roadmap_goal_line_discrepancy.finding: `factory/specs/roadmap.md:113` — the goal line of milestone `csb-audit-1`, and therefore the sentence `smith epic goal-check` compares delivered work against — ends its SEC-2 clause with 'destroying `teamid:` partitions irreversibly — triggered by an ordinary `make app`.' That trailing clause is wrong as written. The mutating call is `scripts/ensure-signing-identity.sh:56`, and lines 23 and 57 put it inside `if ! security find-certificate -c "$SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME" "$LOGIN_KEYCHAIN" >/dev/null 2>&1; then ... fi`. An ordinary `make app` on a machine that ALREADY has the identity — which is every build after the first on that machine — takes the false branch and never reaches line 56.
roadmap_goal_line_discrepancy.proposed_correction: Replace the clause 'triggered by an ordinary `make app`' with 'triggered by an ordinary `make app` on any machine that does not yet have the identity — the call sits inside the `find-certificate` creation branch opened at line 23 — which is every fresh machine, every new user account, and every keychain reset'. One clause, no change to the finding, no change to its severity, no change to the scope of the epic. Proposed only: this planner did not edit `roadmap.md` and will not. The write root for this round is `state/results/csb-audit-1.plan-draft-v4.json` alone, `roadmap.md` is the operator's document, and editing an epic's own goal line is exactly the move that would let a planner quietly widen or narrow what it is later graded against.
roadmap_goal_line_discrepancy.why_this_is_recorded_and_not_fixed: Recorded rather than silently worked around because it has a consumer. `smith epic goal-check` reads this goal line at epic close; a verdict that quotes it quotes the error forward, and the natural reading of the current sentence — that every build detonates — is the kind of overstatement that gets a real S2 discounted the first time someone runs `make app` twice and nothing happens. The severity is untouched: a first build is routine, the identity does not exist on a fresh checkout, and the damage is irreversible whenever it does fire. Note the direction of the error, which is the part that matters for how this is read: the goal line overstates the FREQUENCY and understates nothing about the blast radius. This same fact is load-bearing twice elsewhere in the plan — it is why RISK-8 exists, and it is why task-1's harness may run on a machine where the identity is present without approaching the mutating line. See the ninth `open_questions_for_signoff` entry.

P3.title: Criterion 5(e)'s behavioural launch was worst exactly where it ran most often: CI.
P3.detail: Criterion 12 pins `make signing-test` into CI. A CI runner has no `ClaudeStatusBar Local Signing` identity, so the `find-certificate` probe in `scripts/ensure-signing-identity.sh:23` is FALSE there, and any escape past a non-refusing make-app guard reaches the creation branch — `openssl req`, `security import`, `security set-key-partition-list` — on the runner rather than merely reaching a no-op `source` on the operator's machine. v5's safety argument for build execution rests on nonfunctional clause 2's measured precondition that the identity is PRESENT, and that precondition is a fact about the operator's machine that CI does not share. So the C1 hazard was strictly worse on every automated run than on the developer box.
P3.disposition: Fixed in criterion 5(e) prerequisite (2): the harness re-measures identity presence with a read-only `security find-certificate` immediately before the launch and SKIPS the behavioural half when the identity is absent, printing a pinned skip text; the subcase passes on its static half. This also makes criterion 12's CI invocation honest rather than lucky.

spec_review_r6_disposition._defect_class: F1 and F7 are ONE defect class found independently by two providers on two different tasks: a safety property stated in a clause and asserted by no criterion. F2, F3 and F4 are the adjacent shape — the check is one level narrower (or wider) than the property it must guarantee. v7 fixes the seven instances AND sweeps for the class; the sweep's own two finds are recorded in `planner_findings_v7`.

F1.what_changed: Criterion 4 gains a THIRD CONJUNCT that asserts the expansion operator: every textual reference to `CSB_SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME` must use `-`, never `:-`/`:=`/`=`/`:?`/`?`/`:+`/`+`, with a distinct failing text for the `:-` null and a lengthened pass text. Functional clause 2 now points at that conjunct and says plainly that until v7 it was the only site stating the operator and nothing could fail a diff that ignored it. THE TRADE-OFF THE FINDING LEFT TO THE PLANNER, and the choice: `<SFV>` CONTINUES to admit `${NAME:-word}`. Removing the colon form from the grammar would break the plan's own mandated guard condition `[ -z "${SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME:-}" ]`, which THE GUARD FORM pins character-for-character; `<SFV>` is a test for ABSENCE OF EFFECT and must stay that, while WHICH operator preserves an empty value is a different question at one site. Narrow the site, not the grammar. THIRD CHANGE, defence in depth on the same chain: (B1) now carries the identity-PRESENT prerequisite (B2) already had — if the read-only `find-certificate` probe reports ABSENT, B1 is SKIPPED, not run — plus a criterion-4-green prerequisite. v6 gave that structural protection to B2 and not to B1, which is why F1's chain ended at a real login keychain rather than at a failed assertion.

F2.what_changed: The `(iv-b)` interior-line list no longer contains a shape-only alternative. `a pattern line ending in `)`` becomes `a pattern line matching `<PATLINE>``, and `<PATLINE>` is defined: an optional leading `(`, one or more patterns separated by `|`, a terminating `)` and nothing after it, where EVERY pattern is itself an `<SFV>`. A `$(...)` inside a pattern is now rejected by the same deny-by-default test the rest of the walk uses, instead of being tolerated because the line happens to end in `)`. Applied in both copies of the walk (functional clause 3 and criterion 3).

F3.what_changed: `THE HARNESS LAUNCHES NOTHING ELSE` is replaced by a scoped prohibition plus an explicit permit list. (B) now forbids exactly two things: any invocation of either target script outside (B1), (B2) and (C)'s two builds; and any `/usr/bin/security` MUTATING subcommand (the eight are enumerated) anywhere, on any keychain including a temporary one, with no exception row. It PERMITS by name `/bin/echo`, read-only `security` subcommands, `mktemp`, `env`, the test runner and ordinary read-only text tools, and `codesign`/`swift` where another criterion requires them. This is the third round in which a widening at this site swallowed a sibling requirement (C3 in v5, its fix in v6, F3 now), so the permit list is written down rather than implied.

(1) N5, N6 and M2 are re-phrased against the SHAPE the guard grammar requires — `the guard's exit statement, whatever integer code it carries` — because (g2) admits `exit <N>` for N in 1-255 and a fixture that says `delete the `exit 1`` is unbuildable against a compliant `exit 2`. (2) N2's `at line 23` and N7's `at line 17` become symbolic (`line P`, `line Q`, matched as integers) and both fixtures are now built by locating the construct BY CONTENT, because functional clause 2's own multi-line replacement of line 16 MOVES both. A fixture that fails for the wrong reason trains the worker to weaken the assertion until it passes.

The remaining `task-2 criterion 9` reference is a different task and is correct.

F7.what_changed: Criterion 8 gains probe (g): the pinned source-text match procedure, applied to `verify:` at both sinks — the declaration slice must contain `verify: (String) -> Bool = TrustedApplicationGate.defaultVerify` exactly once, and the whole comment-stripped file must contain that member exactly once (the dead-reference guard). The probe count becomes SEVEN and the procedure's user list becomes (b), (f), (g). Criterion 1's STEP 0 now names the exact default instead of saying `the production verifier`, functional clause 5 points at probe (g), and criterion 6 pins that `the DEFAULT verifier` means `TrustedApplicationGate.defaultVerify` BY NAME so its behavioural probes grade the same member probe (g) proves the sinks bind. CODEX-F4.summary: Criterion 9's static half rejects a compliant fatal handler: `codesign ... --timestamp "$APP" || { echo "timestamped signing failed" >&2; exit 1; }` fails loudly, performs no fallback and satisfies nonfunctional clause 6, but v8 forbade `any ||-joined command on the same logical line`.

THE PERMITTED FATAL HANDLER: a ||-joined continuation is permitted iff its command list ends in an unconditional nonzero exit with no intervening conditional; `|| true`, `|| :`, `|| exit 0`, a logging handler with no exit and a re-signing handler are all forbidden. SONNET-F1.disposition: ACCEPTED-AND-FIXED, BY THE STRUCTURAL OPTION (b) RATHER THAN THE DISCLOSURE OPTION (a)
SONNET-F1.summary: Criteria 8 and 9's new STATIC HALVES are pure-text codesign-line scans with no disclosed residual and are silently inapplicable to a flag-array-indirected codesign invocation. Criterion 8 itself invites the array refactor by requiring one explicit invocation per nested Mach-O; criterion 1's pinned parse routine never resolves a variable or an array expansion, so on `codesign "${SIGN_FLAGS[@]}"` neither `--sign` nor `--deep` nor `--timestamp=none` is present and neither assertion is triggered, while the dynamic halves do not re-derive the signing invocation's own flags.
SONNET-F1.fixed_at: task 1, acceptance_criteria[7] (CRITERION 8, index 7) and acceptance_criteria[8] (CRITERION 9, index 8), plus the shared rule at acceptance_criteria[2] (CRITERION 3, index 2). The reviewer offered (a) append the residual sentence or (b) make an indirected argument list FAIL. v9 does BOTH, and (b) is the load-bearing half: UNRESOLVED IS A FAILURE, NOT A NON-MATCH, with a narrow named exemption for value-position expansions (`"$SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME"` after a literal `--sign`, `"$HOME"`, `"$TMPDIR"`, `"$LOGIN_KEYCHAIN"`, `"${TMPDIR:-/tmp}"`) so the guard does not forbid the identity indirection criterion 3 requires. The residual sentence is added to both static halves as well, because a check that fails an unresolved form still cannot see a `set +e`, a trap, or a sourced wrapper. Negative fixture F-3 must FAIL both criteria.
SONNET-F1.why_both: Option (a) alone leaves the property ungraded and merely honest about it, which is the defect class this epic has been circling since round 7. Option (b) alone leaves the reader with no statement of what remains unseen. The plan's own standing form — THE CLEAN LAUNCH, THE HARNESS INVOCATION INVENTORY — is a structural check PLUS a residual, and that is what criteria 8 and 9 now carry.

P9-Q4.severity_of_this_note: S2-major, and it is a SEVERITY ADJUDICATION rather than a new defect.
P9-Q4.title: P8-P1 and its task-2 mirror P8-P5 are RE-GRADED S1-stop-the-line in v9. The operator may overturn it.
P9-Q4.the_question: The v8 planner graded P8-P1 — the mutating-`security` prohibition that no criterion graded — at S2-major while recording in its own why_not_S1 field that `a case for S1 exists`. Round 9's sonnet observed that every other safety gate of comparable blast radius in this plan (THE GUARD FORM, THE CLEAN LAUNCH, THE MAKE-APP GUARD FORM) is graded S1-stop-the-line, and that open_questions_for_signoff named none of this. Codex's Q4 answer reached the same point from the other end: this is a review adjudication, not a request for permission to relax the prohibition, so it should be resolved and recorded before sign-off rather than deferred into an assent question.
P9-Q4.adjudication: S1-stop-the-line, for both P8-P1 (task 1) and P8-P5 (task 2). Three reasons, in order. (1) BLAST RADIUS AND IRREVERSIBILITY: the ungraded property is the one command whose damage lands on the operator's real login keychain and cannot be undone — `set-key-partition-list` destroys `teamid:` partitions irreversibly, and `delete-keychain` is worse. Every other S1 in this plan protects something recoverable by comparison. (2) CONSISTENCY: grading the epic's own bug, reproduced by the harness written to test it, one rung below the gates that protect the script under test is a ranking no reader can reconstruct from the plan's own stated criteria. (3) IT IS THE ONLY GATE ON A PROHIBITION THE PLAN CALLS ABSOLUTE: nonfunctional clause 1 of task 1 says `the sharpest constraint in this epic`, and a sharpest constraint graded S2 is a sentence with a hedge in it.
P9-Q4.what_changes_operationally: Nothing about the checks themselves — THE HARNESS INVOCATION INVENTORY and THE TEST-SIDE SECURITY INVENTORY are required either way, and both are strengthened in v9 for other reasons. What changes is that a bounce on either is stop-the-line rather than a major finding a wave may carry, and that a waiver against either needs the operator rather than a reviewer.
P9-Q4.recorded_where_the_operator_will_see_it: open_questions_for_signoff entry 10 (index 9) states the decision and that it is theirs to overturn. The v8 records at planner_notes.planner_findings_v8.P8-P1 and .P8-P5 are NOT rewritten — they are what the v8 reviewers actually read — and each carries one appended key `severity_superseded_in_v9` pointing here.

P9-CF2.severity: S3-minor, and it is DISCHARGED in v9 rather than parked again.
P9-CF2.title: The explicit-output convention is applied to task-1 criterion 6 and task-2 criteria 4 and 11 — the open item the v5 planner parked with an explicit handoff that four rounds never saw.
P9-CF2.history: The v5 planner finding P1 recorded that codex's F9 had a trailing clause recommending the convention for these three criteria, declined to act on it (a recommendation is not an acceptance criterion; the turn budget went to the nine confirmed findings), and wrote `It is recorded here so the next round finds it as an open item rather than rediscovering it as a new finding.` The v8 compaction truncated that sentence at 284 characters, so rounds 6, 7, 8 and 9 never saw it. The orchestrator recovered it from the v7 draft as carry-forward CF-2. Round 10 is the round that sentence addressed, four rounds late.
P9-CF2.decision: APPLY, not refuse. The v5 planner's reason for parking was that no reviewer had shown a null-equals-hypothesis defect in those three criteria, which was true then and is a good reason to decline a fourth-hand rewrite. It is a weaker reason in round 10, because rounds 8 and 9 between them established that this plan's failures cluster exactly where a criterion states an obligation without stating the two texts — and because the cost is three appended paragraphs, not a rewrite of criteria a reviewer has already graded.
P9-CF2.applied_at: task 1, acceptance_criteria[5] (CRITERION 6, index 5) — three named checks c6-1..c6-3, each with a hypothesis text and a distinct null text, for a criterion that remains human-graded because there is no mechanical check for a true sentence. Task 2, acceptance_criteria[3] (CRITERION 4, index 3) — c4-1..c4-3, and c4-1 carries TWO distinct nulls, because an all-or-nothing gate and an unfiltered gate are different bugs that v8's text would have reported identically. Task 2, acceptance_criteria[10] (CRITERION 11, index 10) — c11-a, c11-b, plus an explicit BLOCKED text for the case where criterion 12's greps have not matched, so sentence (b) is not written on faith.
P9-CF2.method: APPENDED paragraphs in every case. The existing criterion text is not rewritten, because reviewers in rounds 5 through 9 graded that text and a correction to a graded criterion belongs in an appended note, not in a supersession of the words the grader read.

P9-P1.severity: S3-minor, and it is a DEFECT THIS PLANNER CREATED while fixing CODEX-F1 and F3, filed rather than quietly patched.
P9-P1.title: Permitting inert fixture data is itself an evasion route unless inertness is proven, and permitting `.swift.txt` fixtures under Tests/ is one unless the scan set excludes them by construction.
P9-P1.detail: The fix for CODEX-F1 tells the shell assertions to ignore banned tokens outside executable positions. A coder can then place a live command inside an UNQUOTED here-document, which the shell expands, and call it fixture data. The fix for CODEX-F3 requires never-executed negative fixtures inside the test tree the inventory scans, which would fail the real suite. Both are holes the fix opens.
P9-P1.disposition: Closed in place. Shell: INERT DATA MUST BE PROVABLY INERT permits exactly two shapes — a QUOTED here-document (`<<'EOF'`) writing under `$(mktemp -d)`, or a `readonly` variable used only as a non-passthrough argument — and (p3) makes an unquoted here-document body an EXECUTABLE POSITION, so fixture F-5 `unquoted-heredoc-smuggle` must fail. Swift: fixtures are `.swift.txt` files under `Tests/StatusBarCoreTests/Fixtures/static-assertions/`, never compiled, and every probe's scan set is `.swift` files only, additionally excluding that directory by path — two independent reasons a negative fixture cannot fail the real suite.

P9-P2.severity: S3-minor, DISCLOSED rather than fixed, and it is the residual of v9's own central move.
P9-P2.title: UNRESOLVED IS A FAILURE, NOT A NON-MATCH forbids idiomatic shell that this plan elsewhere requires, and the exemption list is the seam where it can go wrong.
P9-P2.detail: Making an unresolved expansion a FAILURE is what closes SONNET-F1 and the second half of CODEX-F3. But criterion 3 REQUIRES the identity name to reach `codesign` through `"$SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME"`, and the harness necessarily uses `"$HOME"`, `"$TMPDIR"` and `"${TMPDIR:-/tmp}"`-shaped values. So the rule carries a named exemption list for VALUE-position expansions that cannot introduce a flag. If a later revision adds a value to that list without checking that it cannot expand to a leading `-`, the guard weakens silently — which is the same coupling Q2-F1's restored rationale warns about for the WALKER's acceptance set.
P9-P2.disposition: Recorded, not fixed. The exemption list is CLOSED and enumerated in the criterion text; adding to it is a plan revision, not an implementation choice. A later round that needs a sixth exemption should state why the value cannot expand to a flag, in the criterion, at the point of adding it. Recorded here so the next round finds it as an open item rather than rediscovering it as a new finding.

P9-P3.severity: S3-minor, DISCLOSED, and it is the honest limit of v9's fixture requirement.
P9-P3.title: The fixture sets are enumerated by this plan, so they test the assertions against the failures this plan already imagined.
P9-P3.detail: Eleven fixtures in task 1 and nine in task 2 are named, and the fixture run is graded. That converts each assertion from a claim into a measured thing, which is the point. It does not make the assertion complete: a violating shape nobody has thought of is in no fixture and passes every one. The evidence for this is round 9 itself — v8's assertions were sound against every shape v8's author imagined.
P9-P3.disposition: Recorded. The mitigation already in the plan is the standing formula: an implementation that needs a form the checks cannot resolve is a `spec-change-proposed`, not a judgement call, which routes the unimagined shape to a human instead of to a silent pass.

carry_forward_v9.CF-3: STANDING. The v8 compaction removed 31,304 characters across 105 truncated leaf strings, dropping no key and no list entry. Two of those tails are now known to have been load-bearing (CF-1a, CF-1b) and have been restored. The other 103 are UNREVIEWED-BUT-STRUCTURALLY-INTACT and must never be described as certified harmless: the round-9 Q2 reviewer explicitly declined to certify them, because it was shown the removed tails without the surviving prefixes beside them. 103 `[v8-compacted; full text in the v7 draft]` markers remain in this document and are left exactly as v8 wrote them. CORRECTED IN v10 (round-11 finding R11-SONNET-F1, S2-major/correctness): as v9 wrote this note it opened with `35,796 characters across 106 truncated leaf strings` and `the other 104`, and closed with `103 markers remain` — both the wrong number and the right one in one paragraph. The corrected figures are 105 truncated leaves and 31,304 characters, derived by walking v7 against v8 LEAF BY LEAF and summing `len(v7 leaf) - len(v8 leaf)` over the leaves whose v8 value carries the marker; all 105 paths resolve in v7 and none is missing. 105 minus the two restored by CF-1a and CF-1b leaves 103, which is what the closing sentence already said and what `planner_notes_compaction_v9.marker_count_discriminator` already had. THAT NOTE IS CORRECT AND v10 DOES NOT TOUCH IT. RE-MEASURED IN v10 AT THE MOMENT THIS SENTENCE WAS WRITTEN, over this document: 103 leaves TERMINATE in the marker and 2 further leaves contain it without terminating (prose discussing the marker). THE TEST USED, and it is the one that matters: TERMINAL POSITION — a real truncation marker ENDS its string, while prose quoting the marker continues after it. A substring count is the wrong instrument here and returns a number too large by exactly the number of passages that discuss the compaction. THE LESSON, recorded because it will bite this document again as it keeps describing itself: a count of a marker is not a count of the thing the marker marks, once a document has begun to discuss its own markers — a self-describing document poisons its own instrument. Any future count of compaction in this plan must discriminate terminal position, not substring presence, and must state which test it used.
carry_forward_v9.CF-4: STANDING, and it is a method note. Round 9 asked a reviewer whether a compaction lost anything while showing it only what survived; the follow-up showed it only what was removed. Both halves alone are uncertifiable. A question about what a document lost needs the surviving prefix and the removed tail SIDE BY SIDE, plus the operative sections that might already carry the same fact. Any later round that certifies the remaining 104 tails must be given the evidence in that shape or its answer is worthless.

planner_notes_compaction_v9.measurement: planner_notes grew in v9. The round-8 planner reported a compaction while planner_notes NET GREW from 172,227 to 185,529 bytes, because five new live sections outweighed the history they summarised; saying so is the point. v9's before and after byte counts are stated in the planner's return message, measured on the file, not estimated.
planner_notes_compaction_v9.marker_count_discriminator: COUNTING NOTE, because this document now discusses its own markers. A raw text search of this file for the v8 compaction marker returns 106 occurrences. 103 are REAL MARKERS and 3 are PROSE MENTIONS — at plan_version_note, carry_forward_v9.CF-3, and planner_notes_compaction_v9.what_was_done_instead, all three written in round 10 to describe the markers rather than to be one. The discriminator is mechanical and needs no judgement: a REAL marker TERMINATES its string, so the string ends with the marker's closing bracket; a MENTION sits mid-sentence with text after it. Verified by walking the parsed document rather than by grepping the raw bytes: 103 terminal, 3 non-terminal. This is, in miniature, exactly the EXECUTABLE POSITION vs INERT DATA distinction v9 pins for the acceptance criteria — a token that names a thing is not the thing — and it is recorded here so a later round that counts markers with a raw grep gets 106, finds this note, and does not report three phantom truncations.

P10-1.finding: v9's universal verdict `POSITIVE FIXTURES, every assertion must PASS all of them` was ALREADY contradicted by v9's own per-assertion fixture lists, in four criteria, before any reviewer looked at it. Task-1 criterion 1 says its parse `is run against fixtures F+1 and F+2 (must PASS) and F-2 (must FAIL)`; criterion 2 names `POSITIVE FIXTURE: F+1 and F+2`; criterion 8's static half names `POSITIVE FIXTURES it must PASS: F+4 ... and F+1`; criterion 9's names `F+3 and F+4, and F+1`. Each names a SUBSET. A rule and four of its own instances disagreed inside one document.
P10-1.why_it_matters: CODEX-R11-F1 is therefore not a judgement call about strictness; it is an internal contradiction that reading any one of those four criteria beside the class rule would have surfaced. Round 10 wrote the class rule without reading them.
P10-1.action: The applicability table makes the per-assertion lists authoritative and reconciles them with the class rule.

P10-2.finding: The word PASS was overloaded across two incompatible meanings, and the overload is why v9's universal verdict looked reasonable. Task-1 criterion 1 requires EXACTLY ONE `security set-key-partition-list` line and defines a ZERO-match NULL that exits 1 — yet v9 says that criterion's parse `must PASS` against F+1 (the harness's own source), which contains that token only as inert data and from which the parse must select ZERO lines. Under criterion 1's own null, selecting zero IS a failure. So `PASS` at that site cannot mean `the assertion returns its ok text`; it can only mean `the assertion is not fooled by inert data`.
P10-2.action: THE ASSERTION-TO-FIXTURE APPLICABILITY TABLE separates the two meanings into distinct cell values SATISFIED and NOT-FOOLED, and states explicitly that v9's `must PASS` at criterion 1 is to be read as NOT-FOOLED.

P10-3.finding: Both class rules hardcode a fixture COUNT in the same paragraph as the fixture ENUMERATION (`every one of these eleven cases`, `all nine cases`), so any round that adds a fixture silently makes the count wrong while the grading sentence still reads as authoritative.
P10-3.action: Both counts re-derived by enumerating identifiers at the moment of writing and both now state their arithmetic: task-1 15 cases (8 positive, 7 negative), task-2 12 cases (5 positive, 7 negative). A future round adding a fixture must re-derive rather than increment.

P10-4.finding: Every one of the four v10 narrowings widens what a compliant diff may contain, which is the direction that cannot be caught by the fixtures that already exist. F+8 and the four bounds on inert-data shape (iii) are the counter-guards written for exactly this, but they were written by the same planner that widened the rules, so no independent party has tried to smuggle a violation through the new exemptions.
P10-4.action: None available in this round. A round-13 reviewer should attack the widenings adversarially: an `echo` at a second site, a `--sign` operand that expands to a flag, a forwarded argv whose call site is itself assembled, and a YAML probe pointed at a second file.

P10-5.finding: Round 12's own coverage is narrower than the five fixes suggest. Read in full this round: task-1 `acceptance_criteria[0],[1],[2],[5],[6],[7],[8]`, task-1 `contract.functional_clauses[0],[2 partially],[3],[7]`, task-2 `acceptance_criteria[7],[10],[11]` and `contract.nonfunctional_clauses[7]`, `carry_forward_v9.CF-3`, and `planner_notes_compaction_v9`. P10-6.finding: A count of a variable name is not a count of its uses, for the same structural reason a count of a compaction marker is not a count of a truncation: the instrument and the thing measured differ. A bare-dollar search for `$SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME` across task-1 returns 14; including the `${SIGNING_IDENTITY_NAME...}` spelling returns 28. The round-12 dispatch brief carried 15, which is neither, and the discrepancy is an instrument difference rather than a disagreement about the document.
P10-6.why_it_matters: The exemption list this round widened is written in terms of variable NAMES appearing in argument POSITIONS. Any future check that counts or matches those names must state its spelling coverage, or it will silently exempt one spelling and reject the other — which is the same failure shape as CODEX-R11-F2 itself.
P10-6.action: The measured sentence at task-1 `acceptance_criteria[2]` now states its regex, both spellings, and the number a naive search would have returned. Exemptions (e1) through (e3) name the variables individually rather than by pattern.

spec_review_r21_disposition.round: 21 (five findings, each INDEPENDENTLY RE-DERIVED BY THE ORCHESTRATOR AGAINST v14 WITH EVIDENCE QUOTED, not an external reviewer's unverified opinion). Three S2-major (R1, R2, R4) and two S4-nit (R5, NOTE). The freeze rule is not met, so v15 is mandatory rather than optional. All five are actioned below and none is deferred.
spec_review_r21_disposition.the_class: Three of the five (R1, R2, R5) are ONE class, and it is the failure mode this plan's own correction discipline creates. Compiled lesson lesson-dream-dogfood-demo-rpg-1-182 requires a graded criterion to be corrected by an APPENDED note rather than by superseding the words the grader read. Rounds 12 through 14 obeyed that, and the resulting appends RETAINED an old clause and then stated an UNQUALIFIED override of it -- producing a contradiction INSIDE ONE PARAGRAPH, which no precedence clause resolves, because a precedence clause reaches other paragraphs and not its own. v15 keeps the append-only discipline and adds the missing half: EVERY appended sentence in v15 states its own SCOPE -- which clause it overrides, under which condition each governs, and what it explicitly does NOT reach.

R1.claim: v14's exemption sentence -- a here-document whose redirection target is NOT a passthrough REMAINS INERT DATA and fails nothing -- is unqualified as to QUOTING, while retained clause (p3) makes an UNQUOTED here-document body EXECUTABLE with no condition on the receiving command word. For `cat > "$dir/f.sh" <<EOF` the two demand opposite verdicts in the same paragraph. Decisive: required negative fixture (F-5) `unquoted-heredoc-smuggle` must fail by (p3), yet nothing pinned its receiving command word, so one required fixture carried two mandated opposite outcomes and the criterion could not be graded.
R1.action: Appended a scoped correction bounding THE TARGET TEST and the exemption sentence to (p4) and to QUOTED here-document bodies ONLY, and stating that they do NOT bound (p3): an unquoted body is executable whatever its target, because the shell expands it before any redirection delivers it. Named what the exemption does NOT exempt (unquoted here-documents, here-strings, pipes into interpreters, process substitutions). Added the missing nesting rule -- classification applies ONCE, to the OUTERMOST delivery construct, and inert text is NOT re-scanned -- without which the new rule would have failed the harness against its own source under SELF-MATCH IS NOT A VIOLATION. PINNED (F-5)'s receiving command word, which the dispatch expressly permitted: the fixture is DELIVERED by `cat > "$dir/fixture-unquoted-heredoc.sh" <<'EOF'` (quoted, so the harness source stays inert) and the FILE THUS WRITTEN contains `cat > "$dir/inner.sh" <<EOF` with a mutating `security` line inside -- non-passthrough receiver, unquoted body, MUST FAIL by (p3). One fixture, one outcome. Confirmed (n2)'s null construct is quoted, so the (n1)/(n2) text distinction v14 requires survives.
R1.location: tasks[0].acceptance_criteria[2], paragraph 10 of 17 (the EXECUTABLE POSITION vs INERT DATA paragraph). Note the dispatch's coordinates were off by one: the fault sentence is in paragraph 10, not 9, and (F-5) is enumerated in paragraph 14, not 13. Located by content, not by index.

R2.claim: v14 states STAGE 2's roster is the identifier inventory OF THE RUN WHOSE BRACKET SHOWED THE DIFFERENCE and then declares that inventory FINAL unconditionally. Step (2) brackets BOTH the pristine and the post-change run, so the showing run may be the PRISTINE one, whose inventory is BASELINE by construction. The `BASELINE is a SUBSET of FINAL` justification is about COVERAGE OF IDENTIFIERS and is silent about IMPLEMENTATIONS: this task modifies the three test files it claims, so a pristine-bracket difference bisected against the post-change worktree reproduces nothing while the coverage assertion passes in full, and the Result is then permitted to declare the third outcome and assert `an ordering or teardown effect between tests` -- a false cause, in the most likely scenario for this task.
R2.action: Appended a scoped correction splitting the roster rule into two branches SELECTED BY THE BRACKET: (B1) post-change-bracket difference -- re-runs against the POST-CHANGE worktree, roster FINAL, every v14 sentence governing unchanged; (B2) pristine-bracket difference -- re-runs against a tree in the PRISTINE state, roster BASELINE, because a difference produced by pre-change implementations is not reproducible against implementations this task replaced. Stated the override's extent explicitly (v14's FINAL sentence governs (B1) only and is superseded TO THAT EXTENT AND NO OTHER) and handled both brackets differing as two findings. KEPT the coverage assertion, restated against whichever roster the branch selected, and generalised the coverage-shortfall null text to name the roster (`<BASELINE|FINAL>`). Declared (B2)'s own failure mode -- pristine state not reconstructable -> INCONCLUSIVE with its own distinct text plus `spec-change-proposed`, never the third outcome -- and required a pristine-bracket difference to be reported as PRE-DATING this task's changes.

R4.claim: v14's `TASK 1 CLAIMS NO SWIFT FILE, so a one-for-one Swift swap NECESSARILY leaves a modified or added Swift path in that final porcelain listing` is false. `git status --porcelain` compares the working tree with the index and HEAD, so a coder that COMMITTED its work -- the normal end state of a Blacksmith coder task, since the merge queue rebases task branches -- reports an EMPTY porcelain, and the empty set vacuously satisfies `must list only files in this task's claims`. v14 promotes condition (3) to load-bearing while under the normal end state it does no work at all. Verified absences in v14: zero occurrences of `uncommitted`, `staged` or `git diff`, and no reference to `smith claims check`; nothing anywhere required the tree be uncommitted at the final check.
R4.action: Two appends, one repair. (a) In the CITED criterion, added the commit-aware instrument: step (1) additionally records `git rev-parse HEAD` as BASE_SHA at the same moment it asserts the empty baseline porcelain, and step (2) requires BOTH `git diff --name-only <BASE_SHA>` AND `git status --porcelain` to list only claimed paths, with a distinct null text naming the offending paths. The diff listing is empty only if nothing changed rather than empty once committed, so it cannot pass vacuously. Stated that the count equality, the clean-tree baseline and the final porcelain are ALL RETAINED -- this ADDS a listing and relaxes nothing -- and that `smith claims check --since <sha>` MAY be cited as corroboration but what is GRADED is the diff output pasted into the Result, since a criterion must be gradable from the evidence the Result carries (lesson-raised-cbdae7931913: a constraint that holds only because a prompt asked for it is a request, not a limit). (b) In the citing paragraph, corrected `necessarily` to rest on the new instrument and restated the triple's third member as a claim-confined diff THAT SEES COMMITTED WORK, with an explicit scope fence that the paragraph's own subject -- the demotion of the count as task-2's deletion detector -- is untouched.
R4.location: tasks[0].acceptance_criteria[10] (single paragraph) and tasks[1].acceptance_criteria[9], paragraph 2 of 4. No claim was changed: the six claimed paths are enumerated in the added instrument exactly as `tasks[0].claims` already lists them.

R5.verdict: accepted in full, at the graded severity
R5.claim: v14's softened rationale -- `narrow enough that A TIMESTAMP NOT PRODUCED BY THIS PROCESS'S RUN cannot pass` -- is still an overclaim of the same class it was written to fix: a stamp carried over from a run thirty seconds earlier is exactly that, and it passes a 300-second window comfortably. v14's own gloss (`drifts out of range as soon as the calendar moves`) is true of a run long ago and false of a recent re-run.
R5.action: Appended a scoped correction stating what the window ACTUALLY excludes -- a value fixed at authoring time, or any stamp old enough to have drifted out of a 300-second range -- and stopping there, with `IT ESTABLISHES NO PROVENANCE` said in those words. spec_review_r25_disposition.the_class: Three of the six (findings 2, 3 and 6) are ONE class, and it is the failure mode the append-only correction discipline creates at its next level up. v15 fixed the class where an append RETAINED a clause and then stated an UNQUALIFIED override of it, by requiring every appended sentence to state its own SCOPE. v16 and v17 now show the residue: a correction that DOES state its scope can still state it WRONGLY -- an enumeration short by one site (finding 2), a reach clause that contradicts the sentence beside it (finding 3), a declared reach covering 28% of the text it names (finding 6). The rule v17 adds, and which every future version must obey: A CORRECTION MUST DECLARE ITS REACH IN WORDS THAT RESOLVE TO TEXT -- a start phrase and an end phrase, or the clause named by its quoted words -- AND ANY COUNT IT STATES MUST BE MEASURED MECHANICALLY BEFORE IT IS WRITTEN, NEVER EYEBALLED.

F1.claim: Task 2's only claim-confinement assertion grades `no unclaimed edit` with a bare working-tree `git status --porcelain`. Measured on the v16 text (length 7,708): `--porcelain` occurs once, at offset 135; `git diff` zero times; `BASE_SHA` zero times. The defect is threefold and each part is independently disqualifying: it is VACUOUSLY satisfied the moment the coder commits, since a committed change leaves a clean porcelain and the empty set trivially lists only claimed files, so the criterion passes hardest exactly when the most work has been done; it cannot see committed work at all, so it cannot see an unclaimed file edited and committed; and it is blind to a committed rename of an unclaimed path into a claimed one. This is the exact flaw v15 and v16 spent two versions repairing at task 1's site, `tasks[0].acceptance_criteria[10]`. Task 2's site was never repaired.
F1.action: Appended a correction giving this criterion the SAME TWO-PART INSTRUMENT task 1 now carries, mirroring its FORM so the two tasks are graded by one instrument rather than two that drift: a pristine-baseline step that asserts an EMPTY `git status --porcelain` and at that same moment records `git rev-parse HEAD`; an end-of-task `git diff --no-renames --name-only <BASE_SHA_T2>`; the existing final porcelain RETAINED beside it as the uncommitted-tree half of the same condition; the seven claimed paths enumerated; and the task-1 null text mirrored onto task 2's sha. `--no-renames` is required rather than optional because rename detection is on by default (diff.renames true since git 2.9, verified on git 2.55.0) and prints only the destination of a committed rename. THE NAMING FORK WAS DECIDED EXPLICITLY AND THE DECISION IS STATED INSIDE THE CORRECTION: option (a), this criterion captures its OWN base sha in its own step, so it is gradable by a reader who reads nothing else; (a)'s cost, two names for one commit inside one task, is paid off by REUSING the existing name BASE_SHA_T2 instead of minting a second one, with the sha's identity defined IN FULL inside this criterion, pinned by construction (both recordings are `git rev-parse HEAD` on the same pristine tree before the first edit), and protected by a byte-identity null if the Result carries two values. Option (b), referencing criterion 10's BASE_SHA_T2, was REJECTED because it would define this criterion's instrument in a LATER criterion. Scope stated positively: the correction ADDS a baseline step and a second listing and WEAKENS NOTHING; the swift build requirement, the final porcelain, the async-ripple null and every sentence of the test-side security inventory are named as retained.
